chapters.title: Chapter 158 -158-The Master-Servant Pact Between the Human Race and the Godkin
paragraphs: "At last, it’s over."
A faint smile rose on Daniel’s face.
Flash!
Whoosh— He appeared in an instant.
The prodigies of the Empyrean Faction all turned toward him almost at the same time.
There was confusion in their eyes, surprise, and a trace of curiosity.
"A human?"
Kahn frowned, uncertainty coloring his tone.
Daniel arched a brow.
"How could you tell?"
"Heh—"
Kahn let out a disdainful laugh and lifted his chin. "As an overlord race, if we can’t even keep track of the details of our own vassal races, that would be downright laughable."
"Kahn, this human is one of the Godkin’s vassal races?"
"So that makes him one of us?"
"Not necessarily. I don’t think this human came with good intentions..."
Kahn gave a cold laugh. "The Godkin rule over dozens of realms and planes across the cosmos. Among them are human worlds."
He turned and explained to the others beside him.
"This branch of humanity fled here from the Endless Star River. If the Godkin hadn’t ceded a world for them to settle on, they wouldn’t even have had a place to live."
"I see. I was wondering. The human race is at least a second-rate race in the Endless Star River. They’re not exactly struggling. Why would they become a vassal race of the Godkin?"
"Oh, so it’s just one branch of humanity."
Magna of the Netherkin finally understood.
It was just like the Netherkin themselves. Though they all bore the name Netherkin, Magna and Vogan were not from the same exact lineage, which was why they could both enter Heavenscar.
Humanity, in the Endless Star River, was a middling second-rate race—hardly powerful, but hardly weak either. No matter how one looked at it, they shouldn’t have become the Godkin’s vassal race.
This was Daniel’s first time hearing any of this as well.
Kahn looked down at him from above, his tone haughty and overbearing.
"Without the Godkin’s permission, the human race is forbidden from entering Heavenscar. That is an iron rule agreed upon by both races."
"You have already violated that rule by sneaking in here. When I return, I will report this matter to the Godkin..."
At this point, his expression turned icy.
"And when that happens, your people will pay for it."
Daniel’s brows drew together as he asked coldly, "Why are humans not allowed to enter Heavenscar?"
"Hmph!"
Kahn snorted, his face full of contempt.
"Because your race signed a vassal race contract with the Godkin! As a vassal race, if you refuse your master’s orders—are you trying to violate the pact?"
Daniel slowly raised Stellar Wrath and said softly, "Violate the pact?"
"...Until now, I didn’t even know such a humiliating contract existed."
His voice turned cold as sharpened ice.
"But now that I do, so what if I violate it?!"
He sneered.
"What can you do to me?"
Then his smile grew even more scornful.
"What vassal race contract? Just wait. One day, I, Faustus, will march on the Godkin and force you to sign the very same contract!"
"The Godkin shall become the slave race!"
"And humanity shall become the overlord race!"
The moment those words fell, an uproar broke out within the Empyrean Faction.
"Faustus?! So he’s the one who bathed the Holy Palace in blood and assassinated the Holy King?!"
"So it’s that madman! No wonder he looks insane!"
"Exactly! A slave race actually dreaming of breaking the pact unilaterally, even fantasizing about overthrowing the overlord race. How ridiculous!"
"This man is rebellious to the bone. Kahn, if you don’t kill him now, I seriously think he might really go after the Godkin one day."
Kahn’s face darkened to the extreme.
He had never dreamed that the human race would produce such a wild and unyielding prodigy.
Murderous intent surged from him as he said coldly,
"Of course. I’ll kill him right now and leave no future trouble behind."
Quite unexpectedly, Daniel had finally answered some of the questions that had long puzzled him.
So this was the hidden relationship between the Godkin and the human race.
The moment he understood, he wasted no time and summoned all of his clones.
Swish! Swish!—
Ninety-nine clones appeared out of thin air, surrounding the remaining Otherworldly Prodigies on all sides.
"Clones?"
"How laughable."
Kahn sneered in disdain.
His body trembled slightly, and in the next instant, hundreds upon thousands of Kahns appeared simultaneously, packing the sky so densely it seemed to blot out the heavens.
"Repent for your sins!"
Kahn shouted coldly.
Divine radiance burst from the thousand-plus clones, and all kinds of skills rained down on Daniel like a storm.
Daniel’s many clones attacked at the same time as well.
"Hunting Domain!"
"Wind’s Embrace!"
"Shadowfont!"
"Skyfall Strike!"
"Permafrost Prison!"
"Thunder Abyss!"
In a single instant, heaven and earth were overturned.

Countless flaming meteors, trailing long tails of fire, smashed toward the ground. Bone-piercing cold winds froze everything in their path. Across the sky, thunder-element phantoms slaughtered HP without mercy.
Kahn’s skills were just as varied, and their power was no weaker than that of forbidden spells.
But when it came to sustained pressure, he was nowhere near Daniel’s equal.
Endless damage numbers floated above the heads of those Otherworldly Prodigies.
Two prodigies who had already been wounded on the verge of death were killed on the spot.
[Ding! You have killed the prodigy Michael. Obtained Mage Skill Book: "Falling Star" (SSS-Rank), Gold Coins +5,000,000!]
[Ding! You have killed the prodigy Igri. Obtained Warrior Skill Book: "Armor of Holy War" (SSS-Rank), and 115 billion Gold Coins!]
Daniel listened to the system notifications as they rang out one after another.
Flash!
Whoosh!
His figure kept blinking, vanishing, then reappearing again and again.
No matter how many skills Kahn unleashed or how fierce they were, none of them could catch up to Daniel’s speed.

On the contrary, Kahn himself was being bombarded by tens of thousands of continuously active forbidden spells, his HP plummeting in torrents. He had no choice but to keep throwing out Immortal Singularity just to break free from the restraints.
"Damn it! How can this lowly human wield forbidden spells?"
"And why is this bastard so fast?!"
Kahn’s face had turned green.

It wasn’t as if he had never seen forbidden spells before. The Godkin had plenty of powerhouses who could cast them. But never—never—had he seen someone like Daniel, whose forbidden spells were not only instant-cast, but also endlessly spammable.
He couldn’t even imagine how much MP it would take to sustain so many forbidden spells at once.
Was that something a human could possibly do?
By now, Kahn had finally caught the scent of real danger.
He could no longer lie to himself.
He was already standing at death’s door.
If he didn’t bring out his final life-saving trump card right now, he might truly die here today.
"Divine Protection!"
Kahn’s face was black as the bottom of a pot as he finally revealed his last resort.
Within the Godkin, only those with the most monstrous talent were qualified to learn this secret art.

Kahn had mastered it before even becoming a legendary-grade powerhouse, and by now, he had cultivated it to a respectable level. It was strong enough to withstand even a few attacks from a supreme-grade expert.
Whoosh—!
A burst of golden light exploded from Kahn’s body, and in an instant, he transformed into a shining golden statue.
When the forbidden spells struck him, all they produced was a stream of "Miss" notifications.
"As expected of the Godkin. They really aren’t simple."
Daniel frowned slightly, but there wasn’t the slightest trace of panic in him.
Which one of these prodigies didn’t have a few trump cards hidden up their sleeve?
And the Godkin, after all, were one of the great races of the Endless Star River.
The fact that Kahn had been sent into Heavenscar was proof enough that he stood at the top of the Godkin’s younger generation.
Daniel had no interest in wasting time grinding Kahn down. He turned his attention back to clearing out the rest of the prodigies.
This time, he activated Immortal Singularity, and in just a few moves, he sent the already-wounded geniuses to their deaths.
[Ding! You have killed the prodigy Kermos. Obtained Summoner Skill Book: "Hidden Star Descent" (SSS-Rank), Gold Coins +5,500,000!]
[Ding! You have killed the prodigy Hans. Obtained Warrior Skill Book: "Bloodrage" (SSS-Rank), Gold Coins +54 billion!]

sentences.text: "At last, it’s over."
A faint smile rose on Daniel’s face.
Flash!
Whoosh— He appeared in an instant.
The prodigies of the Empyrean Faction all turned toward him almost at the same time.
There was confusion in their eyes, surprise, and a trace of curiosity.
"A human?"
Kahn frowned, uncertainty coloring his tone.
Daniel arched a brow.
"How could you tell?"
"Heh—"
Kahn let out a disdainful laugh and lifted his chin.
"As an overlord race, if we can’t even keep track of the details of our own vassal races, that would be downright laughable."
"Kahn, this human is one of the Godkin’s vassal races?"
"So that makes him one of us?"
"Not necessarily.
I don’t think this human came with good intentions..."
Kahn gave a cold laugh.
"The Godkin rule over dozens of realms and planes across the cosmos.
Among them are human worlds."
He turned and explained to the others beside him.
"This branch of humanity fled here from the Endless Star River.
If the Godkin hadn’t ceded a world for them to settle on, they wouldn’t even have had a place to live."
"I see.
I was wondering.
The human race is at least a second-rate race in the Endless Star River.
They’re not exactly struggling.
Why would they become a vassal race of the Godkin?"
"Oh, so it’s just one branch of humanity."
Magna of the Netherkin finally understood.
It was just like the Netherkin themselves.
Though they all bore the name Netherkin, Magna and Vogan were not from the same exact lineage, which was why they could both enter Heavenscar.
Humanity, in the Endless Star River, was a middling second-rate race—hardly powerful, but hardly weak either.
No matter how one looked at it, they shouldn’t have become the Godkin’s vassal race.
This was Daniel’s first time hearing any of this as well.
Kahn looked down at him from above, his tone haughty and overbearing.
"Without the Godkin’s permission, the human race is forbidden from entering Heavenscar.
That is an iron rule agreed upon by both races."
"You have already violated that rule by sneaking in here.
When I return, I will report this matter to the Godkin..."
At this point, his expression turned icy.
"And when that happens, your people will pay for it."
Daniel’s brows drew together as he asked coldly, "Why are humans not allowed to enter Heavenscar?"
"Hmph!"
Kahn snorted, his face full of contempt.
"Because your race signed a vassal race contract with the Godkin!
As a vassal race, if you refuse your master’s orders—are you trying to violate the pact?"
Daniel slowly raised Stellar Wrath and said softly, "Violate the pact?"
"...Until now, I didn’t even know such a humiliating contract existed."
His voice turned cold as sharpened ice.
"But now that I do, so what if I violate it?!"
He sneered.
"What can you do to me?"
Then his smile grew even more scornful.
"What vassal race contract?
Just wait.
One day, I, Faustus, will march on the Godkin and force you to sign the very same contract!"
"The Godkin shall become the slave race!"
"And humanity shall become the overlord race!"
The moment those words fell, an uproar broke out within the Empyrean Faction.
"Faustus?!
So he’s the one who bathed the Holy Palace in blood and assassinated the Holy King?!"
"So it’s that madman!
No wonder he looks insane!"
"Exactly!
A slave race actually dreaming of breaking the pact unilaterally, even fantasizing about overthrowing the overlord race.
How ridiculous!"
"This man is rebellious to the bone.
Kahn, if you don’t kill him now, I seriously think he might really go after the Godkin one day."
Kahn’s face darkened to the extreme.
He had never dreamed that the human race would produce such a wild and unyielding prodigy.
Murderous intent surged from him as he said coldly,
"Of course.
I’ll kill him right now and leave no future trouble behind."
Quite unexpectedly, Daniel had finally answered some of the questions that had long puzzled him.
So this was the hidden relationship between the Godkin and the human race.
The moment he understood, he wasted no time and summoned all of his clones.
Swish!
Swish!—
Ninety-nine clones appeared out of thin air, surrounding the remaining Otherworldly Prodigies on all sides.
"Clones?"
"How laughable."
Kahn sneered in disdain.
His body trembled slightly, and in the next instant, hundreds upon thousands of Kahns appeared simultaneously, packing the sky so densely it seemed to blot out the heavens.
"Repent for your sins!"
Kahn shouted coldly.
Divine radiance burst from the thousand-plus clones, and all kinds of skills rained down on Daniel like a storm.
Daniel’s many clones attacked at the same time as well.
"Hunting Domain!"
"Wind’s Embrace!"
"Shadowfont!"
"Skyfall Strike!"
"Permafrost Prison!"
"Thunder Abyss!"
In a single instant, heaven and earth were overturned.
Countless flaming meteors, trailing long tails of fire, smashed toward the ground.
Bone-piercing cold winds froze everything in their path.
Across the sky, thunder-element phantoms slaughtered HP without mercy.
Kahn’s skills were just as varied, and their power was no weaker than that of forbidden spells.
But when it came to sustained pressure, he was nowhere near Daniel’s equal.
Endless damage numbers floated above the heads of those Otherworldly Prodigies.

chapters.title: Chapter 159 -159-Killing Kahn by Force, Divine Protection
paragraphs: Daniel swept his gaze across the battlefield. At this point, Kahn was the only one left standing.
Kahn was still maintaining his golden-body state, but Daniel was in no hurry.
If he wanted to, he could keep bombarding him with forbidden spells until the end of time.
But Kahn was in a hurry.
At higher mastery levels, Divine Protection could last for a very long time—but he had not reached that level yet.
By now, he could already feel himself nearing his limit.
Kahn hurriedly spoke up. "Faustus! You dare kill me?"
A cold smile curled at Daniel’s lips.
"What? Only you’re allowed to kill me?"
Kahn grew anxious. "If you kill me, your human race will be abandoned by the Godkin—driven out, perhaps even exterminated!"
Daniel’s eyes sharpened.
The moment Kahn noticed the change in his expression, joy surged through him.
"I am the son of the Godkin Divine King! If you so much as touch a single hair on my head, humanity can wait for divine punishment!"
His calculation was simple enough. Weren’t all Otherworldly Prodigies who came to Heavenscar fighting for the sake of their race?
He refused to believe Daniel could be so selfish that he would disregard the survival of his entire people.
Unfortunately for him, he had miscalculated.
Daniel had lived through the darkest days of humanity in his past lives. He had died several times amid endless catastrophes.
What could possibly be worse than that?
"So this is your threat?"
A cold light flashed in Daniel’s eyes.
Just then, the golden radiance around Kahn abruptly scattered.
Swish, swish, swish—!
Countless forbidden spells engulfed him in an instant.
Boom! Boom! Boom!—
"Pwah!"
Kahn was blasted deep into the earth.
"Faustus! You lowly slave, you dare murder your master?!"
"Your entire human race can wait to be buried with me!"
A moment later, Kahn died.
Daniel smiled and shook his head. Regret?
One day, he would march straight into the God Realm and make those Godkin regret everything before they even had the chance.

They had taken advantage of humanity in its hour of need, forced them into signing a vassal race contract, and then utterly failed to uphold their duty of protection, treating humanity as nothing more than a tool to be used.
The Godkin were courting death.
[Ding! You have killed the prodigy Kahn and obtained the special skill "Divine Protection" (SSS-Rank Forbidden Spell), Gold Coins +9,500,000!]
[Ding! You have killed twelve Otherworldly Prodigies and completed the achievement "Supreme-Grade Heavenly Punishment" — Mission Progress: 2/3!]
[Ding! You have exceeded the requirements for the Heavenscar side mission "Repel the Empyrean Faction’s Assault" and obtained 1,000,000 Fortune Points!]
[Ding! Heavenscar comprehensive evaluation complete. Reward granted to the human race’s Faustus: World Fragment "Aerial Realm"!]
[Ding! Your Fortune Points have exceeded the threshold! Mission difficulty has increased ten thousandfold!]
[Ding! Heavenscar (Mid-Grade) mission has changed. Powerhouses from the Mid-Grade battlefield will descend to the Lower-Grade battlefield to hunt you down. Prepare yourself!]
The rapid succession of system notifications left Daniel a little stunned.
Still, he immediately grasped the key points.
This wave had been an absolute windfall. A massive profit.
At the same time, however, experts from the Mid-Grade battlefield were now going to descend into the Low-Grade battlefield—just to kill him!?
What the hell? Since when was it the Mid-Grade battlefield’s business to interfere in Low-Grade affairs?
[Notice: Your current rank on the Fortune Points Leaderboard has risen to second place!]
Daniel’s eyes flickered.
Originally, he had been dead last on the Fortune Points leaderboard. But after slaughtering all the prodigies, his Fortune Points had skyrocketed.
Humanity’s Fortune Points had surged to one million, earning him an outrageous Fortune Point reward—but it had also pushed him past the threshold limit.
Once the threshold in Heavenscar was exceeded, mission difficulty would rise in proportion to the increase in Fortune Points.
And that, in turn, had caused the upcoming mission difficulty to explode by a factor of ten thousand.
Daniel felt somewhat helpless, but there was nothing he could do about it.
"If they’re coming, then let them come. Who’s afraid of who?"
The harvest from this round was simply insane.
First, he took out a sphere the size of a small watermelon—the fragment of the Aerial Realm.
It was his largest gain, and also the one he had never dared dream of.
A world fragment.
He held the sphere in his hands and examined it closely.
[Aerial Realm (Ultra-Rare · World Fragment)]
Restriction: Exclusive to the human race
Effects:
After use, it can derive a small world from the main world. The contents of that world are generated randomly.
Only the player Faustus may control permissions such as the world entrance and quest system.
The small world can be upgraded and has a chance to mutate.
Upgrade Requirements: World Tree Branch Fragments, World Tree Leaves
Daniel read it over several times, taking several deep breaths before finally suppressing the excitement welling up inside him.
An undeveloped world.
Perhaps it was only a secondary world—but what did that mean?
It meant humanity finally had a territory of its own.
Aetheria was more like land the Godkin had tossed to humanity as alms; humans living there were no different from tenants.
But the Aerial Realm was completely different.
It was territory belonging solely to humanity—the human race’s own homeland, a true dominion that belonged to them and them alone.
Something they could hold firmly in their own hands.
Besides, Aetheria itself was not even a complete plane. At the end of the day, it too was merely a world fragment.
And this Aerial Realm meant that Daniel—and humanity—had just acquired, for free, a brand-new, unexplored Aetheria.
This reward was so absurd it bordered on the outrageous.
"As expected of a gift born from a massive surge in Fortune Points."
Daniel slowly clenched his fist.
This treasure was precisely what those one million Fortune Points had bought him.
He didn’t even dare imagine it—if his Fortune Points ever reached ten million, what kind of heaven-defying reward would descend then?
Taking a deep breath, he pulled out his second piece of loot.
An SSS-Rank Forbidden Spell Skill Book.
[Divine Protection (SSS-Rank Forbidden Spell)]
Effect: After activation, gain the blessing of divine power and become immune to all attacks.
Cost per second: 10,000 points of Immortal Singularity
Note: As the skill level increases, the cost will gradually decrease.
Proficiency: 0 / 100,000
Upgrade Requirement: 0 / 10 SSS-Rank Skill Books
Daniel sucked in a sharp breath.
Invincibility.
Too bad it wasn’t the complete version. Burning ten thousand points of Immortal Singularity per second was a terrifying cost.
Thankfully, it could still be upgraded. At max level, the cost would drop to only one thousand points per second.

The skill had clear limitations, but Daniel currently had Replica Crystals, which could duplicate Immortal Singularity Fragments, so for the time being, he did not need to worry about the consumption.
Still, this was not a long-term solution.
The safest path was to raise himself to Level 100 and fuse with a godhead.
Only after advancing to Legendary Grade would he be able to continuously generate Immortal Singularity on his own.
He immediately designated this as his final life-saving trump card and learned it without hesitation.
[Ding! You have learned the skill "Divine Protection." Your skill bar has been updated.]
He opened his skill menu and, without the slightest hesitation, fed all the SSS-Rank skill books in his possession into it at once, instantly raising it to maximum level.
[Ding! "Divine Protection" has been upgraded to Lv.10 (Max Level)!]
At max level, the cost had dropped to 1,000 Immortal Singularity per second.
He glanced at his inventory. The previous battle had consumed a great deal of Immortal Singularity, and he only had 2,000 points remaining.
In other words, this so-called invincibility would only last two seconds.
As a life-saving trump card, two seconds of invincibility was far too short—especially when Immortal Singularity was needed for other purposes as well.
Without a second word, he pulled out a Replica Crystal and synthesized 394,000 points of Immortal Singularity.
Adding that to what he had left before, he now had a total of 394,200 points.
That meant his invincibility could last for 394 seconds—a little over six minutes of invulnerability.

chapters.title: Chapter 160 -160-Racing Against Time to Destroy the Royal City
paragraphs: The quantity of loot from this round might not have been high, but in terms of quality, it completely eclipsed every previous haul Daniel had ever obtained.
The Aerial Realm alone was already absurdly heaven-defying, not to mention that incomplete version of an invincibility skill.
Daniel had also not forgotten the [Conqueror’s Emblem] he had obtained earlier.
That emblem could ignore all of his personal limits and forcibly raise his damage output to 100 million.
Right now, he was relying on that thing to hold everything together.
But he had a vague feeling that the missions ahead would be far more dangerous.

After all, in the Low-Grade battlefield, even Transcendent Legendary-grade beings seemed to be everywhere. In the Mid-Grade battlefield, perhaps even those at the Transcendent Peak could only serve as cannon fodder.
He would not be the least bit surprised if a whole group of ruthless Supreme-grade monsters descended.
He did not know much about Supreme-grade powerhouses.
Which only made it all the more necessary to arm himself as thoroughly as possible.
Without a second thought, he began upgrading the Conqueror’s Emblem.
[Ding! You are consuming SSS-rank skill books to raise the level of Conqueror’s Emblem. Please confirm.]
"Confirm!"
[Ding! You have consumed an SSS-rank skill book. Conqueror’s Emblem has advanced to Lv.2!]
[Ding! You have consumed an SSS-rank skill book. Conqueror’s Emblem has advanced to Lv.3!]
Then he stopped.
The upgrade mechanism of the Conqueror’s Emblem was viciously demanding.
Every three levels was a major threshold. Once that threshold was crossed, the number of SSS-rank skill books required would multiply explosively.
He glanced at the condition for the next upgrade:
500 SSS-rank skill books!
He opened the Emblem’s status panel.
[Conqueror’s Emblem (Supreme-grade)]
Level: 3
Trait: Growth-type
Effect: After equipping it, all personal limitations are ignored, and all damage dealt reaches 300 million (current upper limit).
Final output is affected by the target’s strength.
Upgrade Requirement: SSS-rank skill books (0/500)
Daniel let out a long breath.
With the upgraded Conqueror’s Emblem, he no longer had any obvious weakness for the time being.
At the opposite pole of Heavenscar...
A towering mountain pierced straight into the clouds, as though it were holding apart the curtain between heaven and earth.
And at the mountain’s highest point lay the legendary summit of Heavenscar—
Cloudcrest Peak.
It was said that only the strongest prodigies in the multiverse were qualified to climb it.
Yet over the course of a thousand years, not a single powerhouse had truly managed to stand upon its peak.
At this very moment, two figures were struggling their way up the mountain.
Judging from their progress, they were still only halfway up.

The one in front was a young man, while the figure one step behind him was Harris, the current number one on the Fortune Points leaderboard and the prodigy of the Starlight Folk, the greatest race in the Endless Star River.
Both of them were breathing heavily.
The youth was slightly better off. He was merely drenched in sweat, as though an entire mountain were pressing down on his shoulders.
But Harris had to stop and catch his breath every few steps, looking as though he was already nearing his limit.
As if by unspoken agreement, neither of them disturbed the other. Their gazes remained locked firmly on the summit.
Only by reaching that place could one truly be acknowledged as the strongest prodigy of this era.
But right then—
[Heavenscar Announcement: The human race’s "Faustus" has repelled the Empyrean Faction’s assault!]
The instant the announcement rang out, both Harris and the young man froze.
The Empyrean Faction had lost?
From ancient times until now, the Empyrean Faction had never once been defeated.
Every round of Heavenscar had always ended in the Empyrean Faction’s victory.
And yet now, the announcement said the Empyrean Faction had been defeated!
Harris’s expression darkened.
"Faustus... who exactly is this bastard?!"
"He was the one who bathed the Holy Palace in blood, and now he’s also the one who stopped the Empyrean Faction’s advance. He certainly knows how to stir up trouble."
But the youth burst out laughing.
He turned back to look at Harris.
"Harris, the price of your arrogance is not small... your Empyrean Faction has suffered a crushing loss!"
The youth shook his head.
If Harris had not rushed off to climb Cloudcrest Peak, and had instead stayed behind to oversee things personally, that Faustus might not have succeeded so easily.
It was precisely because Harris had assumed victory was certain and gone up the mountain alone that he had handed away the chance of winning for free.
"Hmph!"
Harris snorted coldly, chin held high.
"The Starlight Folk possess boundless Fortune Points. What does a minor loss like this amount to?"
He paused, his gaze burning as it locked onto the summit.
"To stand atop Cloudcrest Peak—that alone is what I seek."
"In the Endless Star River, I have crushed every enemy of my generation. Only this final proof is missing."
Reaching the summit of Cloudcrest Peak would be the greatest proof of all.
After saying that, he turned and sneered at the youth.
"And you? Aren’t you, a Supreme-grade Peak expert, also here because you want to make up for the regrets of last time? You’ve climbed this mountain who knows how many times already."
The youth flushed red.
"What would you understand!"
"Back then, in Heavenscar, I simply didn’t participate. If I had gone, I’d have been standing on that summit long ago!"
"Heh."
Harris laughed in disdain and lowered his head to continue climbing.
The youth, having gained nothing from the exchange, did not take it too much to heart. His eyes remained fixed with unwavering determination on the peak disappearing into the clouds.
"Cloudcrest Peak... I, Jonas, will set foot on it no matter what!"
Neither said another word. They simply continued climbing.
[Ding! The pursuers will descend in five minutes! Please prepare yourself!]
Daniel’s eyes sharpened.
Five minutes left!
Those pursuers were the very source of this explosive spike in mission difficulty.
He immediately set off and flew straight toward the Empyrean Royal City.
Above the Empyrean Royal City—
Daniel appeared.
He did not dare waste even a second. If he failed to wipe out the Royal City within those five minutes, then once the pursuers arrived, the mission would become much harder to handle.
He summoned ninety-nine clones, raised Stellar Wrath, and began unleashing skills at the Royal City in a mad torrent.
"Skyfall Strike!"
"Permafrost Prison!"
"Thunder Abyss!"
A sea of forbidden spells exploded across the sky in an instant.
Flames, frost, and thunder engulfed heaven and earth in the blink of an eye.
Bzzzz—!
A protective barrier suddenly unfolded above the Royal City.
Countless forbidden spells were blocked outside it, unable to damage the city in the slightest.
A barrier?
So the difficulty really had increased.
Daniel’s face sank.
There was no time left. He had to end this quickly.
He decisively poured Immortal Singularity into his attacks, amplifying them. With Immortal Singularity’s blessing, the damage instantly increased tenfold!
He bombarded the Royal City like a madman.
Under that terrifying stream of sustained damage, the barrier finally could no longer hold.
Crash!
It sounded like glass shattering.
To Daniel’s ears, that sound was simply beautiful.
"One more minute and I can destroy the Royal City and finish the mission!"
And right then—
[Ding! The pursuers have arrived in Low-Grade Heavenscar!]
The instant the system notification fell, several streaks of light flashed into Daniel’s field of vision.
The pursuers had arrived!
Unwilling to give up, he cast one glance at the Royal City, gritted his teeth, and injected even more Immortal Singularity.
Rumble—!
The entire Empyrean Royal City exploded with a deafening roar, and in the next moment it was reduced to flat ground.
A vast Royal City containing tens of millions of lives, along with countless powerful experts, was erased just like that—as though wiped away by the hand of a god.
[Ding! You have completed the missions "Destroy the Empyrean Kingdom" and "Maintain the Rule of the Holy Kingdom," and obtained 11,000,000 Fortune Points!]
[Ding! Heavenscar comprehensive evaluation complete. Reward granted to the human race’s "Faustus": Special Item "World Tree Seed"!]
Daniel had barely finished listening to the notifications when three terrifying auras that seemed to fill the heavens and the earth suddenly appeared.
They were the auras of Supreme-grade powerhouses.

chapters.title: Chapter 161 -161-Extreme Pursuit and Escape
paragraphs: Swish, swish, swish—!
Three beams of light materialized into three figures, their eyes curiously scanning him.
"Interesting. Truly interesting."
"This is the first time I’ve ever seen someone like you treat us with such disregard."
The one speaking was clearly a Shadowkin warrior.
"Knowing we were coming, any ordinary person wouldn’t even have time to dodge. But he didn’t move at all... is he looking down on us?"
The speaker, a human-looking warrior, had a style completely different from Daniel’s. His entire body was covered in intricate totems.
The last figure was a Woodfolk.
From his appearance, it was evident he was an ape-like being. His face twisted in a savage grin as he slowly approached Daniel.
"It’s been a long time since I’ve seen such a brazen prodigy..."
He raised his head and bared his teeth. "If you can withstand three of my strikes, I’ll spare your life!"
Daniel let out a cold laugh.
Swish, swish, swish—!
His ninety-nine clones suddenly scattered in all directions in a desperate escape.
This was all within the expectations of the three supreme-grade warriors.
A supreme-grade could easily crush a legendary-grade, and to them, Daniel not fleeing would have been madness.
Yet Daniel’s speed far exceeded their expectations—it was almost on par with a typical supreme-grade warrior.
Moreover, every single one of his clones was identical in appearance, leaving them unable to distinguish the real Daniel from his illusions.
"This kid values his life quite a lot."
The Shadowkin warrior chuckled lightly.
The human warrior shook his head. "These little tricks are meaningless."
The two stood still, as if they were merely spectators.
But Kiroli of the Woodfolk tensed suddenly.
He ripped open a rift in the void that stretched over a hundred thousand miles!
A nearly solid arm, spanning tens of thousands of meters, emerged from the rift. Its five fingers blotted out the sky as it swung toward all of Daniel’s clones.
Even with his blinding top-tier speed, Daniel could only move ten thousand miles per heartbeat.
Yet the ape arm’s coverage spanned a staggering one hundred thousand miles!
"Legendary-grade warriors without Divinity... how could they possibly contend with a supreme-grade opponent?"
The human warrior laughed easily.
The Shadowkin warrior observed with interest. "Indeed, the gap between legendary-grade and supreme-grade is as vast as heaven and earth."
"The key difference is that we possess Divinity, while legendary-grade warriors do not. Kiroli’s Divinity, however, is not specialized in tracking—it excels in direct combat."
On the other side, Daniel manipulated the movements of his clones using mind power.
He had already clearly sensed the spatial anomaly, particularly the oppressive force that weighed heavily on his chest, making it hard to breathe.
[Ding! You are now within the Divinity of supreme-grade warrior Kiroli!]
Divinity!
Daniel’s expression changed dramatically.
He knew little about supreme-grade warriors, but he was not entirely ignorant.
In his previous lives, he had reached the pinnacle of legendary-grade, touching the threshold of Divinity.
Only a legendary-grade warrior with Divinity could step into supreme-grade.
Of course, this was after the fusion of game and reality.
Otherwise, in the game alone, merely leveling up repeatedly could eventually make one supreme-grade, without needing to breakthrough on one’s own.
Divinity also required the support of Immortal Singularity to maintain.
The "Ultimate Assassin" title Daniel had previously obtained was essentially a minor form of Divinity.
Within a specific area, it granted overwhelming advantages, drastically weakening enemies.
But compared to true Divinity, it was like a firefly against the full moon—insignificant.
At that moment, he suddenly sensed a dangerous aura!
Without hesitation, he cast his newly learned forbidden spell: "Divine Protection!"
Swish, swish—!
Several of his clones halted abruptly, their bodies instantly coated in dazzling golden light.
Kiroli’s massive hand descended with a roar, snatching those clones into his palm.
Yet several other clones were still fleeing desperately!
Kiroli snarled in rage.
"Damn it! This kid is cunning! You two aren’t just spectators—help me catch him!"
The Shadowkin and human warriors exchanged glances, both showing surprise.
Kiroli’s prowess among supreme-grade warriors was considerable, yet he still couldn’t capture this kid?
Their expressions turned serious. In an instant, they transformed into streaks of light and pursued Daniel’s remaining clones.
Kiroli stared at the clones within his Divinity, frustrated.
"Divine Protection!?"
"Damn, what connection does this kid have with the Godkin..."
He could not break through this invincible buff, but he couldn’t afford to let the clones go.
If the real Daniel was hidden among them, he would be laughed at.
Gritting his teeth, he opened his massive maw wide—stretching over a thousand meters—and swallowed those clones whole.
Then he unleashed his mind power, covering a hundred thousand miles, and pursued with streaks of light.
Daniel did not dare slow down.
[Ding! You consumed Immortal Singularity!]
Boom!
His speed surged explosively, generating a deafening sonic boom.
The effects of Immortal Singularity were miraculous—revival and regeneration were just basic applications.
It could infinitely boost attack power, stack layers of defense, maximize weapon and armor potency, and naturally, enhance speed to lightning-fast levels.
Now, Daniel was using Immortal Singularity purely for acceleration, leaving the three supreme-grade warriors dumbfounded.
Such wastefulness of a rare resource was unheard of, even for them.
But Daniel had no time for hesitation.
At that moment, an idea for escape flashed in his mind—Cloudcrest Peak!
That mountain was the closest and contained a unique suppressive power—it was his only chance to shake off his pursuers.
He commanded the remaining clones and sped toward Cloudcrest Peak.
Within a few breaths, the majestic peak loomed in the distance.
"Faster, faster!"
[Ding! You consumed Immortal Singularity!]
[Ding! You consumed Immortal Singularity!]
He frantically pushed his speed to the limit, leaving the three supreme-grade warriors stunned.
"Damn it, how much Immortal Singularity has this kid stockpiled?"
"He isn’t even legendary-grade—where is all this divinity coming from?"
"No, he’s trying to reach Cloudcrest Peak!"
Cloudcrest Peak—a sacred place in the boundless galaxy where countless prodigies proved themselves.
Legend said only those who reached the summit were worthy of the title "Unrivaled of Their Generation."
The three supreme-grade warriors immediately panicked.
"No, we can’t let him reach it, or it’ll be a disaster!"
"Cloudcrest Peak has special restrictions; any warrior stepping in has their power suppressed."
"The weaker your strength, the lighter the suppression; the stronger you are, the heavier the suppression."
"Back in the day, we couldn’t even hold out halfway up. Didn’t expect we’d face this again today."
"That damned brat! If I catch him, I’ll make him pay!"

chapters.title: Chapter 162 -162-Surpassing the Predecessors, Outpacing Two
paragraphs: Cloudcrest Peak.
Boom!
Daniel plunged headfirst into the towering mountain.
For the first time, he allowed himself a small sense of relief.
"Keep going up!"
He didn’t dare relax for even a moment. Entering this area didn’t guarantee absolute safety.
To be truly safe, he had to reach the summit!
Coincidentally, his class change quest required nothing more than reaching the top.
At the foot of the mountain, he hadn’t felt much pressure, and so he dashed upward recklessly.
Whether he could actually reach the summit... he gritted his teeth.
"Summit means survival; fail to reach it, and it’s death!"
Meanwhile, the three supreme-grade warriors were in pursuit.
Seeing Daniel climbing, their expressions instantly fell.
This majestic mountain bore harsh seals left by ancient supreme beings.
The stronger one was, the heavier the suppression they suffered.
Conversely, the weaker one was, the looser the restraint.
Now, the three supreme-grade warriors at the mountain’s base found their proud Strength advantage turned into a burden.
Catching Daniel here was almost impossible.
"Should we continue striking to kill him?"
Kiroli glanced sideways at his companions.
The Shadowkin warrior shook his head slowly.
"Fighting here would consume every ounce of our Strength a thousandfold compared to the outside."
"Exactly. If we expend too much here, we’ll never catch him."
The human supreme-grade warrior also voiced his objection.
Kiroli snorted coldly. "So we’re reduced to chasing him on foot?"
"At the moment, yes. Just do our best. The rewards and penalties for this quest aren’t severe—do what we can, leave the rest to fate."
The three supreme-grade warriors came to a decision: they had no choice but to climb the mountain.
But soon, they realized they were not the only ones ascending the peak.
"Jonas?!"
Kiroli exclaimed in surprise.
"This guy always stirs up trouble in the mid-grade battlefields. Every time he gets a privilege, he comes to climb this mountain."
The human warrior smiled.
"That should be Harris, the prodigy of the Starlight Folk."
"Heard he’s been noticed by the gold-grade Sacred Mountain, groomed to become a rising star of the new generation."
His tone carried open admiration.
"Harris only needs to step into supreme-grade to reach the Astral Ranking. Then all factions will notice him. That gold-grade Sacred Mountain has keen foresight, moving first."
Kiroli’s face showed disdain.
"So what’s so impressive?"
"It’s just relying on a prestigious background. If I were a Starlight Folk, I’d be stronger than Harris!"
The other two shook their heads repeatedly.

The universe was never fair. The Starlight Folk, as the apex race, produced only a few individuals each generation. But over time, they could awaken ancient bloodlines and inherit ancestral legacies, soaring to become the strongest of their era.
Other races simply couldn’t compare.
Meanwhile, Daniel looked back.
The three supreme-grade warriors had indeed caught up—but their speed was still slower than his.
His heart eased slightly.
Although he didn’t fully understand the mysteries of Cloudcrest Peak, he reasoned:
If reaching the summit was this difficult, there must be special restrictions.
As it turned out, his gamble had paid off.
He didn’t linger on speculation, continuing to climb with focus.
But the higher he went, the more he felt an invisible force dragging at his limbs.
Opening his attribute panel, all his stats appeared normal.
Yet the suppressive power was undeniably real.
He shook his head and pressed on.
After a while, fatigue set in.
His legs felt as if bound by invisible chains, every step requiring immense effort.
Up ahead, not far from him, two other figures were struggling upward.
"Harris?"
He didn’t know them personally, but the Empyrean Faction’s prodigies had mentioned one of them—a remarkably powerful individual.
Even so, their pace was far slower than his.
Daniel was slightly surprised.
Though exhausted, he was still moving with considerably less strain than the two ahead.
Jonas was near his limit, drenched in sweat as if he had just been dragged from water.
Harris fared no better, gritting his teeth, veins bulging on his forehead.
Yet, no matter the difficulty, neither showed the slightest hint of giving up. They persevered relentlessly.
Seeing this, Daniel’s mind stirred.
Isn’t life like this?
The more treacherous the path ahead, the more one must grit their teeth and endure.
A great warrior never yields easily.
Just like himself, living another life carrying the regrets and unfulfilled ambitions of his previous ones.
He was willing to stake everything for the fate of humanity—no matter the setbacks, he would keep moving forward.
He continued his ascent.
Soon, he surpassed Harris.
Huh?!
Harris stared blankly at Daniel’s retreating back, his mind in utter disbelief.
After all his struggles, he had been overtaken by a latecomer?!
It was inconceivable.
Moreover, the one surpassing him was a prodigy of the same generation.
He had been revered as "Unrivaled of His Generation," and this "same generation" spanned the entire universe, not just a single world!
Yet this suddenly appeared human prodigy overtook him with such ease.
Harris could hardly believe his eyes.
"What kind of joke is this?"
"Who is he, really?"
"Could he be... Faustus?"
The moment he was surpassed, his composure nearly collapsed.
Jonas also noticed someone overtaking Harris behind him.
Yet he himself could not take another step.
Hands pressed to the ground, gasping for air, he suddenly forced a smile.
"Harris, what face do you have left to claim you’re the pinnacle of your generation?"
"This person must be Faustus. Tsk tsk... how does it feel to be humiliated like this?"
Harris’s face flushed red, his lips coldly curling, while a bitter taste of envy rose in his chest.
Daniel glanced back curiously at Harris as he heard Jonas speak.
Indeed, this was Harris.
But surpassing him didn’t stir any strong emotions in Daniel.
It was only natural—nothing worth remarking.
After all, Harris had moved so slowly.
However, that other young man seemed even slower.
Daniel casually glanced at him, then pushed forward a few steps, leaving Jonas behind as well.
Uh...
Jonas stared blankly at Daniel effortlessly overtaking him.
His face burned like he had been slapped across the face.
"No way! This human... overtook me so easily?"
"This is absurd!"
He gave a bitter laugh, watching Daniel’s figure grow distant.
"Hmph, and you still dare to criticize me?"
"I thought you were impressive, but you’ve been surpassed too!"
Behind him, Harris’s voice carried a gloating tone.
Yet his eyes remained locked on Daniel, filled with jealousy and unwillingness to yield.

Boom!
Daniel plunged headfirst into the towering mountain.
For the first time, he allowed himself a small sense of relief.
"Keep going up!"
He didn’t dare relax for even a moment.
Entering this area didn’t guarantee absolute safety.
To be truly safe, he had to reach the summit!
Coincidentally, his class change quest required nothing more than reaching the top.

"Summit means survival; fail to reach it, and it’s death!"

chapters.title: Chapter 163 -163-The Brightest Star
paragraphs: Watching Daniel surpass the two ahead, the three supreme-grade warriors at the foot of the mountain were shocked.
"Am I seeing things? That kid actually overtook Harris?"
"Impossible... he even left Jonas behind!"
"My heavens... what is he? He’s already climbed nearly two-thirds of the way up!"
"From the looks of it, there’s no way the three of us can catch him."
The three supreme-grade warriors exchanged glances, a deep sense of helplessness flashing in their eyes.
Even reaching Jonas’s position was impossible for them, let alone catching Faustus.
It was a fool’s dream.
"Heh, isn’t that Jonas?"
"Weren’t you dominating the mid-grade battlefield? Then why don’t you go chase Faustus!"
Kiroli mocked with a sharp remark.
Jonas cast a glance at the foot of the mountain, his expression grim.
"If you provoke me, none of you will return alive."
Then he turned his gaze back toward Daniel—and unexpectedly smiled.
"Harris has no hope of reaching the summit. Faustus, huh?"
"Then let’s see if you can work a miracle and reach Cloudcrest Peak!"
"Even if I can’t summit myself in this life, witnessing a prodigy reach the peak is an honor."
In that instant, his obsession with reaching the summit dissipated considerably.
Instead of worrying whether Daniel could make it, he found himself filled with anticipation.
After all, for over a thousand years, no prodigy had set foot on that supreme-grade peak.
If Faustus succeeded, he would be the number one of his generation!
Daniel’s steps grew heavier and heavier, climbing as slowly as an old man in twilight.
At this moment, he was still tens of thousands of meters from the summit, untouched for a millennium.
Yet he did not stop.
Thirty-nine thousand meters... thirty-one thousand... twenty thousand!
He exhaled deeply and glanced back.
Harris was still trailing behind, struggling. The prodigy of the Starlight Folk had begun burning Immortal Singularity, using his divinity as fuel to power each agonizing step.
Yet his pace was painfully slow, each step consuming vast amounts of Immortal Singularity.
At this rate, once his divinity ran out, he would come to a halt.
Daniel shook his head, withdrew his gaze, and pressed forward.
The last twenty thousand meters proved far more arduous than the previous three hundred thousand.
It was as if he were dragged into an invisible swamp, every limb gripped tightly by an unseen force.
Each step forward consumed a hundred times the usual effort.
Seventeen thousand... fifteen thousand... thirteen thousand!
Stomp!
Crack!
He gritted his teeth as his bones groaned under the immense pressure.
With each step, his skeleton felt as though it were breaking and reforging over and over.
"No wonder this peak has remained unconquered for a thousand years..."
He muttered to himself, then his gaze sharpened.
"Immortal Singularity!"
Without hesitation, Daniel ignited his Immortal Singularity.
In an instant, the invisible shackles binding him shattered, and the mountain-like Strength suppressing him dissipated.
He felt as light as a swallow.
It worked!
Step, step, step!
His pace quickened, racing toward the summit.
Halfway up, the three supreme-grade warriors watched Daniel’s agile ascent, their eyes wide with astonishment.
"If Faustus can maintain this momentum, he will reach the summit," the Shadowkin warrior said gravely.
"But he doesn’t have that much Immortal Singularity to waste. Historically, all summit conquerors only ignited it in the final ten thousand meters to surge to the top."
"Don’t treat Faustus as an ordinary prodigy."
The human warrior shook his head.
"Indeed. First he used Divine Protection, then frantically burned Immortal Singularity to accelerate. Even we supreme-grade warriors can’t match the extent to which he’s using it."
"Tsk tsk... what we call extravagance may be just a trifle to Faustus."
"True. I’ve never seen such a transcendent being before."
"Let’s just watch and see if he can make it to the top."
Ten thousand meters behind Daniel.
Harris was still burning Immortal Singularity, but the flames had dulled, flickering like a dying candle in the wind.
He watched Daniel’s figure, his expression increasingly complex.
The Starlight Folk possessed the fastest Immortal Singularity refinement speed in the entire galaxy, and could store far more than any other race.
Yet now, he doubted his own racial advantage.
Were the Starlight Folk really the strongest race in the universe?
If so, how could he explain this human?
He wasn’t even legendary-grade, yet he wielded Immortal Singularity with flawless mastery, enduring for so long...
All of this was happening right before his eyes.
Harris felt his worldview collapsing.
"With Faustus’ momentum, if he can maintain it... maybe he really can reach the summit!"
Confronted with this fact, his heart was filled with frustration.
Suddenly, a thought occurred to him.
Perhaps Faustus was so unimpeded precisely because he had not yet stepped into legendary-grade—the suppression was smaller, so his progress was smoother.
"Sigh... the stronger one is, the heavier the obstacles."
"No wonder most historical summit conquerors were legendary-grade low-grade, or even epic-grade or Exalted-grade prodigies."
"I can’t summit... because I’m too strong?"
Harris was proud, but now his pride was crushed.
In any era, usually only one prodigy could reach the summit. Some eras had none.
Harris was born in this era. He had believed with absolute certainty that he would be the one to ascend.
That belief was ingrained in his bones.
But now, his belief was shattered.
Another prodigy existed in this era, one above him.
A mysterious human—Faustus.
Harris lifted his gaze.
The distance between him and Faustus had grown even greater.
"Sigh..."
He let out a bitter sigh.
Fifteen thousand meters behind Daniel.
Jonas had long since stopped.
The one known among supreme-grade warriors as "the strongest" had finally relinquished his long-held obsession.
Before encountering Faustus, summiting Cloudcrest Peak had been his undying desire.
From weakling to mighty, from epic-grade to the pinnacle of supreme-grade, he had exhausted every method to reach that mountain.
Why such obsession?
Because his era was a broken one. No one in his generation had conquered Cloudcrest Peak.
It was a monumental humiliation.
A ridicule of an entire generation of young prodigies.
He knew that no matter how his generation would later dominate the galaxy, they could never erase the mark of being the "weakest generation."
Thus, he wanted to obliterate that mark.
For a thousand years, he had climbed again and again, with a life consumed by battle and ascent.
Yet even then, he never succeeded.
The mountain had always been there, yet he could never reach the summit.
The feeling was more suffocating than death itself.
Yet, after meeting Daniel, he felt a sense of release.
"When an era abandons you, it doesn’t even say goodbye."
He exhaled deeply.
Their era was over, like a dream that would never return.
Life was full of regrets, just like his undying obsession with the summit.
"Faustus, show me the glory of your generation."
He watched the figure ascending ever closer to the peak and whispered:
"Climb... reach the summit...
Proclaim to the galaxy that you are the brightest star among the stars!"

chapters.title: Chapter 164 -164-Reaching the Summit of Cloudcrest Peak, the Morning Star!
paragraphs: By now, Daniel’s forehead was drenched in sweat.
He continued burning Immortal Singularity, yet every step still felt incomparably difficult.
The summit was right ahead.
Five thousand meters... three thousand... two thousand...
He panted heavily as he climbed upward step by step.
He could clearly sense that the rate at which his Immortal Singularity was being consumed had suddenly increased severalfold.
At this rate, in just a few more seconds, his Immortal Singularity might be completely exhausted.
"I can’t stop here... the summit is already within reach."
Daniel suddenly came to a halt.
From his backpack, he took out Replica Crystals and Immortal Singularity Fragments.
Though only the final two thousand meters remained, he knew that the closer he got to the summit, the more frenzied the consumption of Immortal Singularity would become.
He did not know how those prodigies of the past had managed to reach the peak. Perhaps each had possessed their own unique talents and divine arts.
But he knew one thing clearly: if he did not replenish his Immortal Singularity right now, he would likely never be able to take those final few steps.
Without hesitation, he synthesized 400,000 points of Immortal Singularity!
"Move!"
Boom—!
The dim light around his body suddenly flared up again, blazing like a torch and illuminating the mist around the summit.
Charge!
In one breath, he rushed toward the peak!
Under the mountain-like pressure, Daniel suddenly broke into a run.
The flames around him were like the only light in a world of darkness—so dazzling, so impossible to look at directly.
One thousand meters... seven hundred... two hundred...
Harris, who had been keeping his eyes fixed on Daniel the whole time, stopped climbing.
Jonas widened his eyes, staring blankly at that mass of flame drawing infinitely close to the summit.
Halfway up the mountain,
the three supreme-grade powerhouses gazed at Daniel’s figure with mixed emotions.
"So the most dazzling prodigy of this generation... has appeared in such a fashion?"
the Shadowkin powerhouse murmured.
"We came here to hunt him down, yet instead we’ve become witnesses to his making history,"
the human powerhouse said with a soft laugh.
"This kid is truly different. If he’s allowed to grow, he will become the nightmare of every powerhouse in the endless worlds!"
"If we get the chance... we still have to kill him completely!"
Kiroli said darkly.
The other two supreme-grade powerhouses fell silent.
Kiroli was right.
The endless galaxy had always been a place of brutally tangled interests. Even the three of them had once fought each other to the death.
It was only because their strengths were so close that none of them could kill the others.
And now, they had a common enemy.
In Daniel’s vision, the summit was now so clear it seemed close enough to touch.
Only forty meters remained!
But at that moment, the burning speed of Immortal Singularity abruptly exploded, becoming a hundred times faster!
"Just hold on a little longer!"
"The mission will be complete soon!"
"For humanity, I absolutely cannot fall here..."
His eyes were bloodshot, streaked with red veins.
With every step he took, he could feel a massive amount of Immortal Singularity draining away at terrifying speed.
"For humanity, so they may no longer suffer endless calamities!"
Thirty meters left!
"For humanity, so they may have the freedom to roam the endless galaxy!"
Ten meters left!
"For... survival!"
Only one step remained!
Daniel was already standing at the edge of the summit.
Before him was the final step.
Step onto it, and he would reach the top!
He slowly raised his leg...
At that moment—
Boom!
Daniel’s foot came crashing down onto that final step.
Whoosh!
A dazzling burst of light erupted from his body, enveloping him completely.
In the next instant, he appeared upon a lofty platform wreathed in drifting clouds and mist.
Beneath his feet stretched an endless sea of clouds!
This... was Cloudcrest Peak!
"So this is... what it means to reach the summit?"
Daniel came back to himself and looked down.
Through the gaps in the sea of clouds, he could take in the full expanse of the land below at a glance. The smallness of all living beings was laid bare before his eyes.
[Ding! You have completed the class change mission "The Light of Humanity"! Please submit the mission as soon as possible.]
Reaching the summit of Cloudcrest Peak was one of the final objectives of the class change mission.
Now that all three objectives had been completed, he only needed to return and turn in the mission to obtain the new-version unlock scroll and the forbidden-grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll.
[Ding! You have obtained the achievement "Rising Star of the Era"! You have received the special items "Phantom Emporium (supreme-grade)," "Earth Elemental Core," and "Light Elemental Core"!]
Listening to the system notification, Daniel let out a long breath.
There was no need to say much about the Elemental Cores—they were tied to unlocking that Chronoverse Prologue Codex.
He had already collected three Elemental Cores before. With these two added, this made the fifth.
Once he gathered all ten, he would obtain the forbidden power of the Laws of Time and Space.
Still, there was no rush in that matter.
He turned his gaze toward the other reward—Phantom Emporium.
After receiving the Millionfold Boost, this achievement reward had actually ascended into a transcendent special item.
[Phantom Emporium (supreme-grade)]
Effect: Can spawn phantoms within a designated area. Range: 10000 × 10000
Number of phantoms: 10,000
Refresh frequency: Once every 60 minutes
Maximum phantom rank: transcendent legendary-grade
The level cap increases as the world version advances. Killing phantoms grants normal drops.
Special: The user possesses full authority and may freely adjust the strength of the phantoms.
Description: A mysterious ancient relic of unknown origin, greatly enhancing the strength of adventurers.
Daniel nodded slightly.
This item was essentially an endlessly refreshing trial ground.
The key point was that the strength of the phantoms could be adjusted freely. If given to players, it could raise their combat power to an entirely new level in an extremely short time.
He put the item back into his backpack.

[Ding! On behalf of humanity, you have claimed supreme glory. Humanity has been rewarded with 15,000,000 Fortune Points! You have received a Fortune Points reward: special item "Ancestral Totem (???)"!]
[Ding! Your Fortune Points have risen to first place on the Fortune Points Ranking!]
Daniel’s gaze flickered.
This wave of Fortune Points rewards had directly pushed humanity to the top of the ranking, suppressing Harris of the Starlight Folk into second place!
And this Fortune Points reward itself seemed anything but ordinary.
He took out the totem scroll that radiated an ancient aura.
[Ancestral Totem (???)]
Level: ???
Rank: ???
Effect: Can be used in the world of your own race, immediately granting [Ancestral Sanctum] ×100, [Ancestral Monument] ×100, [Ancestral Sacred Statue] ×100.
[Ancestral Sanctum]: Suppresses all non-human races within a radius of ten thousand meters! Immovable.
[Ancestral Monument]: Each monument can offset 100 points of lost racial Fortune Points.
[Ancestral Sacred Statue]: Each statue can manifest one ancestral sage of the race for 6 hours.
Daniel read it word by word, and for a long time his heart could not calm down.
His luck was simply too heaven-defying—he had actually obtained such a treasure!
This reward was of immeasurable importance.
With it, even if humanity were pushed into desperate straits, they would never be exterminated.
At the very least, they would possess a pure land that could not be invaded.
For the humanity of his previous lives, something like this was beyond even their wildest dreams.
This gain could not be measured by any standard of value.
Just then,
the final system notification sounded.
[Ding! You have reached the summit of Cloudcrest Peak! Achievement completed: [Astral Morning Star]. Would you like to initiate a wide-area broadcast?]

sentences.text: By now, Daniel’s forehead was drenched in sweat.
He continued burning Immortal Singularity, yet every step still felt incomparably difficult.
The summit was right ahead.
Five thousand meters... three thousand... two thousand...
He panted heavily as he climbed upward step by step.
He could clearly sense that the rate at which his Immortal Singularity was being consumed had suddenly increased severalfold.
At this rate, in just a few more seconds, his Immortal Singularity might be completely exhausted.
"I can’t stop here... the summit is already within reach."
Daniel suddenly came to a halt.
From his backpack, he took out Replica Crystals and Immortal Singularity Fragments.
Though only the final two thousand meters remained, he knew that the closer he got to the summit, the more frenzied the consumption of Immortal Singularity would become.
He did not know how those prodigies of the past had managed to reach the peak.
Perhaps each had possessed their own unique talents and divine arts.
But he knew one thing clearly: if he did not replenish his Immortal Singularity right now, he would likely never be able to take those final few steps.
Without hesitation, he synthesized 400,000 points of Immortal Singularity!
"Move!"
Boom—!
The dim light around his body suddenly flared up again, blazing like a torch and illuminating the mist around the summit.
Charge!
In one breath, he rushed toward the peak!
Under the mountain-like pressure, Daniel suddenly broke into a run.
The flames around him were like the only light in a world of darkness—so dazzling, so impossible to look at directly.
One thousand meters... seven hundred... two hundred...
Harris, who had been keeping his eyes fixed on Daniel the whole time, stopped climbing.
Jonas widened his eyes, staring blankly at that mass of flame drawing infinitely close to the summit.
Halfway up the mountain,
the three supreme-grade powerhouses gazed at Daniel’s figure with mixed emotions.
"So the most dazzling prodigy of this generation... has appeared in such a fashion?"
the Shadowkin powerhouse murmured.
"We came here to hunt him down, yet instead we’ve become witnesses to his making history,"
the human powerhouse said with a soft laugh.
"This kid is truly different.
If he’s allowed to grow, he will become the nightmare of every powerhouse in the endless worlds!"
"If we get the chance... we still have to kill him completely!"
Kiroli said darkly.
The other two supreme-grade powerhouses fell silent.
Kiroli was right.
The endless galaxy had always been a place of brutally tangled interests.
Even the three of them had once fought each other to the death.
It was only because their strengths were so close that none of them could kill the others.
And now, they had a common enemy.
In Daniel’s vision, the summit was now so clear it seemed close enough to touch.
Only forty meters remained!
But at that moment, the burning speed of Immortal Singularity abruptly exploded, becoming a hundred times faster!
"Just hold on a little longer!"
"The mission will be complete soon!"
"For humanity, I absolutely cannot fall here..."
His eyes were bloodshot, streaked with red veins.
With every step he took, he could feel a massive amount of Immortal Singularity draining away at terrifying speed.
"For humanity, so they may no longer suffer endless calamities!"
Thirty meters left!
"For humanity, so they may have the freedom to roam the endless galaxy!"
Ten meters left!
"For... survival!"
Only one step remained!
Daniel was already standing at the edge of the summit.
Before him was the final step.
Step onto it, and he would reach the top!
He slowly raised his leg...
At that moment—
Boom!
Daniel’s foot came crashing down onto that final step.
Whoosh!
A dazzling burst of light erupted from his body, enveloping him completely.
In the next instant, he appeared upon a lofty platform wreathed in drifting clouds and mist.
Beneath his feet stretched an endless sea of clouds!
This... was Cloudcrest Peak!
"So this is... what it means to reach the summit?"
Daniel came back to himself and looked down.
Through the gaps in the sea of clouds, he could take in the full expanse of the land below at a glance.
The smallness of all living beings was laid bare before his eyes.
[Ding!
You have completed the class change mission "The Light of Humanity"!
Please submit the mission as soon as possible.]
Reaching the summit of Cloudcrest Peak was one of the final objectives of the class change mission.
Now that all three objectives had been completed, he only needed to return and turn in the mission to obtain the new-version unlock scroll and the forbidden-grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll.
[Ding!
You have obtained the achievement "Rising Star of the Era"!
You have received the special items "Phantom Emporium (supreme-grade)," "Earth Elemental Core," and "Light Elemental Core"!]
Listening to the system notification, Daniel let out a long breath.
There was no need to say much about the Elemental Cores—they were tied to unlocking that Chronoverse Prologue Codex.
He had already collected three Elemental Cores before.
With these two added, this made the fifth.
Once he gathered all ten, he would obtain the forbidden power of the Laws of Time and Space.
Still, there was no rush in that matter.
He turned his gaze toward the other reward—Phantom Emporium.
After receiving the Millionfold Boost, this achievement reward had actually ascended into a transcendent special item.

Effect: Can spawn phantoms within a designated area.
Number of phantoms: 10,000
Refresh frequency: Once every 60 minutes
Maximum phantom rank: transcendent legendary-grade
The level cap increases as the world version advances.
Killing phantoms grants normal drops.
Special: The user possesses full authority and may freely adjust the strength of the phantoms.
Description: A mysterious ancient relic of unknown origin, greatly enhancing the strength of adventurers.

This item was essentially an endlessly refreshing trial ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 165 -165-Godkin’s Wrath Spreads Across the Stars
paragraphs: Daniel paused for a moment to think.
With so many powerful beings witnessing this, hiding it was pointless.
Better to declare it openly to the world:
I, Faustus, have surpassed the prodigies of all worlds and ascended Cloudcrest Peak!
Even the Endless Worlds will have to swallow their pride!
"Yes!"
Aetheria.
[World Announcement: Player "Faustus" has reached the summit of "Cloudcrest Peak"—becoming the contemporary "Astral Morning Star"!]
Boom—!
The world announcement blared abruptly.
All players froze in astonishment.
"Faustus is invincible! Wait, what great feat has he pulled off this time?"
"No idea, but it sounds impressive—Astral Morning Star, tsk tsk!"
"Astral Morning Star? So majestic!"
"Honestly, if I could be even half as strong as him, I’d be satisfied."
God Realm.
In the towering God Realm, the gods sat upon their cloud-throne, solemn and immovable.
Countless deities simultaneously heard a single name ringing in their ears:
"Human, Faustus!"
"Is this the one responsible for killing my Godkin prodigy, Kahn?"
"How dare the humans rebel, slaying the prodigies of my kind! Unforgivable!"
"He must not be allowed to grow! Crush him now!"
"This branch of humanity has gone beyond our control—they must be annihilated!"
Demon Realm.
In the shadows of the endless abyss,
countless demon gods once again heard that now-familiar name.
"Faustus? The human prodigy who suppressed my Shadowkin faction and guards the rift of the abyss?"

"Aetheria was once the territory of the Demon Realm in ancient times. The God Realm lured humanity to oppose us, suppressing my Shadowkin for ten thousand years—this is a grudge that cannot be forgiven!"
"Faustus must die! He cannot be allowed to grow, or the Demon Realm will be in grave danger!"
"This matter requires long-term planning. Aetheria is only a fragment of a world; a Divine-grade warrior cannot intervene."
Low-Grade Heavenscar.
Jonas gazed upward at the solitary figure atop the clouds, eyes flashing with admiration.
"I am actually witnessing the birth of the Astral Morning Star of this generation... Faustus, truly radiant!"
"Only a prodigy like him could ever reach the peak."
He lowered his gaze, a bitter smile tugging at his lips.
"I was wrong."
He had long since lost the most precious Strength.
Swish—his figure vanished, leaving only a faint, lingering sigh.
"Time waits for no one..."
Harris stared unblinkingly at Cloudcrest Peak.
His gaze held envy, jealousy, and a profound awe.
He was the prodigy closest to Faustus.
He had witnessed, step by step, how Faustus climbed to the summit.
If it had been him, there would have been no way to reach that height.
It was proof enough: Faustus was far beyond him.
Harris focused intently on that figure, as if trying to imprint the image into his very bones.
All the turbulent emotions swirling in his heart suddenly faded, leaving only burning battle intent.
"Faustus! I have a premonition—we will meet in battle very soon."
A faint smile curved his lips.
"I will await your arrival somewhere in the Endless Galaxy."
Swish—!
His figure disappeared as well.
Halfway up the mountain, the three supreme-grade warriors who had already given up the chase stood silently.
They had witnessed firsthand how a prodigy ascended Cloudcrest Peak, bathing in supreme-grade glory capable of shaking the entire Endless Galaxy.
"From now on, the name Faustus will spread across the stars."
"Find the world he lives in!"
"Such a dazzling prodigy—better to eliminate him sooner rather than later."
"Undoubtedly, many more than just us now seek his life. Countless factions likely wish to put him to death."
"Forget it. This mission has failed completely. Let’s return and accept our punishment."
Swish, swish, swish—!
Three figures broke through the air and vanished into the horizon.
[Ding! You have completed all missions in "Low-Grade Heavenscar." Would you like to teleport back to Aetheria immediately?]
Daniel listened to the message echoing from the void, a faint smile lifting the corners of his lips.
"Teleport."
He felt the light and shadows warp before him, the galaxy reversing its flow.
When his vision cleared, he found himself standing upon the land he knew so well: Aetheria.
Daniel surveyed the surroundings, looking at the cities and skies that carried countless memories of his battles and reincarnations, and a long-forgotten sense of peace welled up in his heart.
"It’s time to submit the class change mission."
As the sole hidden class change mission for the forbidden-grade archer, this trial’s reward was entirely different from anything he had encountered before.
The part that stirred his heart most was the legendary "New Version Unlock Scroll."
He was eager to see whether the upcoming game version would be like those in his previous lives.
Thinking this, he stepped into the portal, heading straight to Luminara.
Luminara, Hall of the Profession Mentors.
[Ding! Congratulations on completing the class change mission "The Light of Humanity."]
[Ding! You have obtained "New Version Unlock Scroll" ×1 and "forbidden-grade archer (unique) Class Awakening Scroll" ×1.]
The system message echoed in Daniel’s ears.
At this moment, each of his hands held a scroll emanating an ancient glow.
He carefully placed the New Version Unlock Scroll, which would determine humanity’s fate, into his pack.
Then, he tore the Class Awakening Scroll—bearing the glory of the forbidden-grade archer—into the air.
In the next instant, the fragments transformed into golden sparks, like fireflies, merging into his body.
[Ding! Congratulations! Class change successful!]
[Notice: Your level cap has been removed; you may continue leveling.]
Daniel immediately began leveling up.
[Ding! Level up! Current level: 161. Attribute points gained: 20.]
[Ding! Level up! Current level: 167. Attribute points gained: 20.]
[Ding! Level up! Current level: 170. Attribute points gained: 20.]

[Notice: You have not completed the next stage of the class change mission. The level cap remains sealed. Overflowing experience is temporarily stored in the EXP pool. Complete the class change promptly to lift the level cap.]
After leveling, Daniel allocated all free attribute points to Agility.
Because he wore Attribute Replication equipment, his other stats rose proportionally.
At that moment, Mentor Shadow Song sent a golden light into his forehead.
[Ding! Do you accept the forbidden-grade archer class change mission "Form the Holy Angel Legion"?]
Daniel paused briefly, then decisively responded.
"Accept!"
[Ding! You have accepted the class change mission "Form the Holy Angel Legion"! Your task log has been updated; check for details.]
Daniel opened the task log.
[Form the Holy Angel Legion] (forbidden-grade archer class change mission)
Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Objectives:
Find the entrance to the Angelic Realm.
Recruit at least 100 Holy-Winged Angels.
Train at least 100 Holy Crusader Angels.
Mission Background:
In ancient times, humanity and the Angel race were both old civilizations on Aetheria.
To secure land for survival, human ancestors fought angels, suppressing the Shadowkin.
However, the third-generation Angel King, Vakaciri, unexpectedly obtained a world fragment and led the entire angel race into it, naming it the "Kingdom of Heaven."
The entrance to this angelic realm is said to remain hidden in a void rift within Aetheria, only becoming visible after the new game version unlocks.
Mission Duration: Long-term
Mission Rewards: Fountain of Life, forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll
