chapters.title: Chapter 166 -166-A Minor World for Humanity Alone
paragraphs: After reading through the quest interface, Daniel immediately understood.

So that was how it had happened—back then, the Angel King had also obtained a World Fragment, and that was how he had opened up the Angel Plane, a realm independent from the continent yet still faintly connected to it.
When the new version descended, the gate leading to the Angel Plane would appear.
A faint smile rose to Daniel’s lips, but deep down, a trace of concern lingered in his heart.
The reason was simple enough: his relationship with the angel race could hardly be called friendly.
The moment he killed the angel prince, he had thoroughly offended the Angel King.
"But if I remember correctly, I still have an Angelic Sacred Crystal on hand?"
It was an ancient token he had obtained all the way back in the novice stage.
According to its description, whoever possessed it could make one wish to the Angel King.
"I just hope that when the time comes, that Angel King will be smart enough."
Daniel smiled.
A wise man knew when to yield to circumstances.
Whether he made a wish or not was secondary. As long as it let him enter the Angel Plane, that would be enough.
As for how he would complete the quest after entering the Angel Plane, he was not worried in the slightest.
He had plenty of methods at his disposal, and even more confidence in his own strength.
With that thought, he did not immediately take out the Scroll of Version Upgrade from his inventory.
Before that, there was still one more thing he had to do first.
World Fragments!
The class advancement quest had stated it clearly.
It was precisely because the Angel King had obtained a World Fragment that he had been able to create the Angel Plane.
"World Fragments... I have one as well."
Daniel stepped out of the Hall of Classes, activated Voidstep, and shot straight up into the sky, climbing a hundred thousand meters into the air.
Only after he came to a halt above the sea of clouds did he solemnly take out the "Aerial Realm" World Fragment.
[Ding! Do you wish to use the "Aerial Realm" World Fragment?]
[Notice: Once the command is given, it cannot be reversed. At the same time, "Aerial Realm" will randomly evolve into a brand-new world.]

[Warning: You only possess the authority to issue quests within this world and to enter or leave it. If you wish to truly control the entire world, you must personally conquer the native inhabitants of this plane.]
After hearing the system’s warning, Daniel felt no ripple in his heart.
A randomly evolved world would inevitably be occupied by indigenous life.
If he wanted to completely claim this land, he would have to conquer the native forces within it.
Once he understood that point, he was entirely at ease.
He had been able to conquer Aetheria—so why would he fear this?
Not to mention that he also held in his hands the Fourth Calamity—
the endless player army, fearless, deathless, and ever surging forward!
When the time came, all he had to do was issue a single quest, and the overwhelming tide of calamity would drown the entire Aerial Realm.
That would be the true descent of "calamity."
There was simply too much room for manipulation here.
Perhaps, compared to merely owning a ready-made world, the benefits he could seize this way would be even greater.
"Use it."
Daniel did not hesitate.
[Ding! You have used the "Aerial Realm" World Fragment!]
[Ding! You have activated and unlocked the "Astral Realm" system interface.]
[World Announcement: Player "Faustus" has successfully activated the "Astral Realm" interface. All players may now access this interface to view the details of the "Astral Realm."]
Listening to the system notifications, Daniel opened the [Astral Realm] interface.
Whoosh—
A vast and boundless Star Chart unfurled before his eyes.
Yet the chart was dim and obscure. Only two spherical stars—Aetheria and Aerial Realm—were lit brightly. Every other direction was shrouded beneath a dense layer of fog.
He tried tapping on the icon for Aetheria.
[Aetheria (Minor World)] (World Fragment)
Rank: Beginner
Authority: None
Affiliated Faction: Godkin
Current Power Cap: transcendent legendary-grade
Required for Upgrade: Scroll of Version Upgrade
Daniel did not continue reading.
He already knew all of this by heart.
At once, he clicked on Aerial Realm.
[Aerial Realm (Minor World)] (World Fragment)
Rank: Beginner
Your Authority: Pioneer (Upgradeable)
Affiliated Faction: Human Race
Current Power Cap: transcendent legendary-grade
Required for Upgrade: World Tree Broken Branch, Remnant Pages of the Genesis Scripture...
Note: This world is currently in the process of evolution. Progress: 10%... 21%... 35%...
Daniel read through the detailed description of Aerial Realm word by word, then compared the two worlds side by side, immediately spotting many differences.
Among them, the most crucial distinction was this:
Aetheria belonged to the Godkin.
But Aerial Realm belonged to humanity.
At that thought, he suddenly remembered another reward still lying in his inventory.
[World Tree Seed (???)]
Originally, he had intended to use this seed on Aetheria.
But now he had changed his mind.
The World Tree Seed had to be used on Aerial Realm.
Because Aerial Realm was the true territory that belonged to humankind alone.
Daniel took out the seed from his inventory. It radiated an ancient aura of life.
[World Tree Seed (Unknown Grade)]
Level: 1
Grade: ???
Usage: Can be planted in any [Plane of Life]—

Effect 1: As the seed sprouts and grows, the territory of the world it resides in will continue to expand, its spatial structure will become increasingly stable, and the world’s rank will rise accordingly.
Effect 2: As the seed grows, all living beings within that plane will gain an additional source of [Mystic Origin Power].
Effect 3: As the tree becomes more lush and flourishing, all beings of that plane will awaken more—and stronger—talent potential.
Requirements for Advancement: Life Sacred Spring ×10, Sacred Soil ×10, Holy Spirit Servant ×10

Record: In the ancient legends of the endless river of stars, the laws of time and space condensed into the [Cosmic Tree], and the Cosmic Tree was the source of all origins. It transformed into countless World Tree Seeds, evolving into worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. It is said that every great world possesses a complete World Sacred Tree...
After reading this, a sharp light flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
Of course he knew what a Plane of Life was.
Any world capable of nurturing life could be called a Plane of Life.
Which meant that both Aetheria and Aerial Realm met the conditions for planting it.
Moreover, the World Tree Seed had the property of growth.
As it grew, the entire world would grow alongside it.
The World Fragment would gradually become more complete, and from there continue evolving.
Perhaps one day, it might even grow until it became as vast and magnificent as the God Realm occupied by the Godkin.
As for the materials required for advancement...
He remembered that the rewards for the class advancement quest included Life Sacred Spring.
In that case, the upgrading of the World Tree Seed would not be a problem for the time being.
However, Aerial Realm was still in the middle of its evolution, so there was no need to rush.
It would not be too late to plant it after Aerial Realm finished evolving.
He put the World Tree Seed back into his inventory.
At present, there were still two urgent matters that needed to be handled.
The first was the [Ancestral Totem], which he had yet to use.
Daniel planned to use this supreme treasure on Aetheria.
If he did that, it would mean the human race possessed two world territories.
He was not worried in the slightest that the Godkin would come to suppress or drive them out.
He knew full well that this minor world simply could not withstand the descent of a Divine-grade powerhouse.
As for the possibility of the God Realm sending supreme-grade experts to invade, he felt no fear at all.
As long as he pushed the world’s version forward, it would not be long before Aetheria gave birth to a batch of supreme-grade powerhouses of its own.
If the God Realm dared send troops into Aetheria, then he dared cut them down with a single blade.
That was his confidence.

sentences.text: After reading through the quest interface, Daniel immediately understood.

So that was how it had happened—back then, the Angel King had also obtained a World Fragment, and that was how he had opened up the Angel Plane, a realm independent from the continent yet still faintly connected to it.
When the new version descended, the gate leading to the Angel Plane would appear.
A faint smile rose to Daniel’s lips, but deep down, a trace of concern lingered in his heart.
The reason was simple enough: his relationship with the angel race could hardly be called friendly.
The moment he killed the angel prince, he had thoroughly offended the Angel King.
"But if I remember correctly, I still have an Angelic Sacred Crystal on hand?"
It was an ancient token he had obtained all the way back in the novice stage.
According to its description, whoever possessed it could make one wish to the Angel King.
"I just hope that when the time comes, that Angel King will be smart enough."
Daniel smiled.
A wise man knew when to yield to circumstances.
Whether he made a wish or not was secondary.
As long as it let him enter the Angel Plane, that would be enough.
As for how he would complete the quest after entering the Angel Plane, he was not worried in the slightest.
He had plenty of methods at his disposal, and even more confidence in his own strength.
With that thought, he did not immediately take out the Scroll of Version Upgrade from his inventory.
Before that, there was still one more thing he had to do first.
World Fragments!
The class advancement quest had stated it clearly.
It was precisely because the Angel King had obtained a World Fragment that he had been able to create the Angel Plane.
"World Fragments...
I have one as well."
Daniel stepped out of the Hall of Classes, activated Voidstep, and shot straight up into the sky, climbing a hundred thousand meters into the air.
Only after he came to a halt above the sea of clouds did he solemnly take out the "Aerial Realm" World Fragment.
[Ding!
Do you wish to use the "Aerial Realm" World Fragment?]
[Notice: Once the command is given, it cannot be reversed.
At the same time, "Aerial Realm" will randomly evolve into a brand-new world.]
[Warning: You only possess the authority to issue quests within this world and to enter or leave it.
If you wish to truly control the entire world, you must personally conquer the native inhabitants of this plane.]
After hearing the system’s warning, Daniel felt no ripple in his heart.
A randomly evolved world would inevitably be occupied by indigenous life.
If he wanted to completely claim this land, he would have to conquer the native forces within it.
Once he understood that point, he was entirely at ease.
He had been able to conquer Aetheria—so why would he fear this?
Not to mention that he also held in his hands the Fourth Calamity—
the endless player army, fearless, deathless, and ever surging forward!
When the time came, all he had to do was issue a single quest, and the overwhelming tide of calamity would drown the entire Aerial Realm.
That would be the true descent of "calamity."
There was simply too much room for manipulation here.
Perhaps, compared to merely owning a ready-made world, the benefits he could seize this way would be even greater.
"Use it."
Daniel did not hesitate.
[Ding!
You have used the "Aerial Realm" World Fragment!]
[Ding!
You have activated and unlocked the "Astral Realm" system interface.]
[World Announcement: Player "Faustus" has successfully activated the "Astral Realm" interface.
All players may now access this interface to view the details of the "Astral Realm."]
Listening to the system notifications, Daniel opened the [Astral Realm] interface.
Whoosh—
A vast and boundless Star Chart unfurled before his eyes.
Yet the chart was dim and obscure.
Only two spherical stars—Aetheria and Aerial Realm—were lit brightly.
Every other direction was shrouded beneath a dense layer of fog.
He tried tapping on the icon for Aetheria.
[Aetheria (Minor World)] (World Fragment)
Rank: Beginner
Authority: None
Affiliated Faction: Godkin
Current Power Cap: transcendent legendary-grade
Required for Upgrade: Scroll of Version Upgrade
Daniel did not continue reading.
He already knew all of this by heart.
At once, he clicked on Aerial Realm.
[Aerial Realm (Minor World)] (World Fragment)
Rank: Beginner
Your Authority: Pioneer (Upgradeable)
Affiliated Faction: Human Race
Current Power Cap: transcendent legendary-grade
Required for Upgrade: World Tree Broken Branch, Remnant Pages of the Genesis Scripture...
Note: This world is currently in the process of evolution.
Progress: 10%...
Daniel read through the detailed description of Aerial Realm word by word, then compared the two worlds side by side, immediately spotting many differences.
Among them, the most crucial distinction was this:
Aetheria belonged to the Godkin.
But Aerial Realm belonged to humanity.
At that thought, he suddenly remembered another reward still lying in his inventory.
[World Tree Seed (???)]
Originally, he had intended to use this seed on Aetheria.
But now he had changed his mind.
The World Tree Seed had to be used on Aerial Realm.
Because Aerial Realm was the true territory that belonged to humankind alone.
Daniel took out the seed from his inventory.
It radiated an ancient aura of life.

Level: 1
Grade: ???

chapters.title: Chapter 167 -167-Mutation! A Completely Different New Version!
paragraphs: Aside from using the Ancestral Totem, the second urgent matter was to open the new version!
In his previous lives, Daniel had gone through several version updates before the game finally merged with reality a year later.
Opening a new version also meant providing players with more gameplay systems and more paths for growth.
It was an inevitable step.
Daniel steadied himself and decided to handle things one by one.
He directly took out the [Ancestral Totem].
Once this item was deployed, the human race on Aetheria would stand on unshakable ground.
Whether it was the [Ancestral Temple] or the [Ancestral Statue], both possessed the power to suppress non-human races.
As for the [Ancestral Monument], it could slow the loss of the human race’s Fortune Points.
[Ding! Are you sure you want to use the [Ancestral Totem]?]
"Confirm!"
Daniel took a deep breath.
[Ding! Successfully used! Obtained [Ancestral Temple] ×1,000,000, [Ancestral Monument] ×1,000,000, [Ancestral Statue] ×1,000,000!]
The corners of Daniel’s lips curled upward.
Bzzzz—
The totem scroll in his hand suddenly trembled, letting out a deep humming sound.
Daniel released his grip.
The [Ancestral Totem] instantly transformed into countless golden motes of light, scattering toward every corner of Aetheria!
Standing high in the sky, he saw it clearly.
Some streaks of golden light landed and became [Ancestral Temples], some became [Ancestral Monuments], and some became [Ancestral Statues].
Golden radiance rained across every inch of the continent.
That meant wherever the golden light touched, it would become an invincible territory of the human race!
Even if the myriad races invaded in the future, humanity would no longer have to fear the disaster of extinction!
Immediately afterward, Daniel took out the [Scroll of Version Upgrade].
He did not know whether history had already been rewritten because of his existence.
Nor did he know whether the next version would be the same as in his previous lives.
But no matter the outcome, he feared nothing.

Now, with the NPC and player resources of two great World Zones under his command—on top of the strength he had accumulated by carving his own path forward—he was more than capable of facing any challenge.
[Ding! Do you wish to use the "Scroll of Version Upgrade"? Please note: after using this scroll, the game’s progress will be updated to a new version!]
[Notice: After the new version opens, none of the current players’ data will be affected, but the current world will undergo major changes. All details must be explored by the players themselves.]
Daniel said in a low voice, "Use it!"
[Ding! You have used the [Scroll of Version Upgrade]. The new version, [Flame of Heritage], has been unlocked!]
At the same time—
[Server Announcement: Player "Faustus" has successfully unlocked the new game version [Flame of Heritage]!]
[World Announcement: The brand-new version [Flame of Heritage] has officially descended!]
[Notice: Brand-new changes will take place in the new version. Players, please explore them on your own!]
All the players across Stellar were caught completely off guard by the sudden announcement.
The moment they heard it was Faustus again, discussion instantly erupted.
"Boss Faustus always does this—changes this backward world in the blink of an eye, hahaha..."
"Boss Faustus is invincible, but what I want to know is, will the new version affect my leveling?"
"Boss Faustus, can the new version unlock a companion system?"
"Holy shit, bro, finding a partner has nothing to do with the version. That’s on you."
"I’m talking about legally partnering with non-human races..."
"Wait... hold on. Boss Faustus can manually unlock game versions too? Isn’t this kind of thing supposed to be updated automatically by the system?!"
"This is beyond ridiculous! I’m still stuck in the Starter Village trying to figure out how to do my class change, and the boss has already overturned the entire world’s progression..."
Players had always been naturally adaptable.
They were eternally curious about anything new, and utterly fearless.
However, when Daniel heard the name of the new version, his brows furrowed slightly.
[Flame of Heritage]?
In all his previous lives, there had never been a version by that name!
He took a deep breath.
This world had truly changed because of him.
There had already been signs of it throughout the game’s many progression stages.
And this time, it was no longer just a matter of the pace accelerating—a completely new version, one that had never appeared before, had descended.
But no matter what lay ahead, no matter what hardships he encountered, he would do as he always had:
crush every enemy that dared lay a hand on humanity.
He did not think of himself as saving anyone.
He simply did not want the regrets of his previous lives to repeat themselves.
Human civilization should not have to struggle like this.
Nor should it end in total annihilation.
At that thought, Daniel smiled.
Just then—
[Ding! "Aerial Realm" evolution complete!]
Hm?
Daniel blinked.
The completion of Aerial Realm’s evolution meant he could now step into this world that belonged solely to humanity.
"I’ll go take a look first. Once the time is right, I’ll let the players enter."
He opened the [Astral Realm] interface and clicked on "Aerial Realm."
After finding the entrance, he chose to enter without hesitation.
[Notice—you have arrived in "Aerial Realm"! ]
[Ding! You have discovered "Aerial Realm." Contribution Points +1,000,000!]
Daniel’s figure appeared within Aerial Realm.
This was a world that felt as though it had only just been born!
Suspended high in the heavens, he looked down over this land reserved exclusively for humanity.
He saw an azure sky, pure white clouds, and breathed in the fragrance of grass and trees drifting through the air...
He even saw countless animals roaming freely across this world!
Their forms were wildly varied, and most of them were enormous in size.
Some were birds with wingspans stretching tens of thousands of meters.
Others were four-legged beasts like moving mountain ranges.
Now that the world had only just been born, these creatures treated this land as their own home...
running and soaring as they pleased.
Daniel frowned slightly.
If a world were ruled by only a single species—especially a species without civilization—it would be an absolute disaster for that world.
He flew above one of the beasts and casually cast a detection spell.
[Hornless Rhino] (low legendary-grade)
Level: 200 (world cap)
Rank: legendary-grade
Skills: [Bloodline Surge], [Mountain Trample], [Heaven-Shaking Roar], [Soul Shadow]...
Drops:
[Blood Crystal] — has a chance to grant inheritance of an ancient beastfolk bloodline after use
[Gemstone] — a crystal containing mysterious energy
[Beast Soul] — a rare material used for forging divine weapons

Description: A native lifeform unique to Aerial Realm, divided into two major branches: herbivores and carnivores, scattered across every corner of the world. After their bloodlines awaken, they can generally reach legendary-grade. The current world limit is god-grade, Transcendent Peak. They stand at the top of Aerial Realm’s food chain. Their entire bodies are treasure; for specific drops, please check after killing them.
After carefully reading through it, Daniel gained a general understanding of the animals of Aerial Realm.
The drops from these creatures alone were already incredibly tempting.
What was more, they did not contain Immortal Singularities.
Instead, the beastfolk bloodlines within them possessed some of the same effects as Immortal Singularities!
In an instant, a bold idea arose in Daniel’s mind regarding these creatures.
To other players, this would practically be a shortcut to godhood!
At that moment, he directly started viewing these animals as livestock raised on his own land.
What he did not know, however, was that while he was observing them, they were also observing him.
Roar!
Rrrgh...
The beasts let out uneasy, low growls in his direction.

chapters.title: Chapter 168 -168-The Hornless Rhino — Treasure from Head to Toe
paragraphs: "Let’s first see how strong these native beasts really are."
This was Daniel’s first time coming into contact with these creatures, and he did not yet understand how they fought.
Understanding their combat patterns would determine how he would formulate grinding strategies for players in the future.
So he was in no hurry to make a move.
He deliberately lowered his altitude and hovered right in front of the beasts, looking at them the way one might inspect pigs or dogs.
At once, the caution in the lead Hornless Rhino’s eyes turned into towering fury.
A flash of blood-red light burst from its body as it charged straight at Daniel!
Its massive frame was unimaginably huge, and at this moment it came crashing forward like a mountain rolling over the earth.
Daniel remained in an observational state the entire time.
The instant the blood-red glow appeared on the Hornless Rhino, all its stats truly doubled.
"So this is how the beastfolk bloodline is used?"
At the same time—
"Flash!"
Whoosh—
Without the least hurry, he blinked a short distance away and lightly evaded the charge.
Roar! Roar!
The Hornless Rhino flew into a rage and shook its body violently.
In the void, a phantom identical to its true form—but much smaller—suddenly appeared.
Whoosh—
The phantom shot toward Daniel like lightning, far lighter and far faster than the main body!
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Could this phantom be the [Beast Soul]?
"Not bad."
He smiled and teleported again.
No matter how the phantom pursued him, he could always dodge with ease.
A few minutes later, he felt that was enough.
This creature probably had no other attack methods left.
Daniel glanced at the Hornless Rhino below him, instantly summoned ninety-nine clones, and swung Stellar Wrath!
"Hunting Domain!"
"Shadowfont!"
"Wind’s Embrace!"
"Thunder Abyss!"
Boom—!
Boom—!
A deafening peal of thunder exploded as hundreds of forbidden spells poured down like a raging tide, instantly swallowing the colossal beast whole.
In barely the blink of an eye—
[Ding! You have killed [Hornless Rhino], obtaining [Blood Crystal] ×10,000, [Gemstone] ×10,000, [Beast Soul] ×10,000!]
Hearing the system notification, Daniel took out the drops for a closer look.
After all, the Hornless Rhino’s description had not explained the true uses of these spoils in detail.
He first picked up a crimson crystal about the size of a pebble.
[Blood Crystal (legendary-grade)]
Level: Tier 1
Rank: legendary-grade
Effect: After use, there is a 1% chance of obtaining a [beastfolk bloodline], thereby gaining the corresponding race’s [Bloodline Inheritance].
[Bloodline Inheritance]: Allows one to transform into an ancient beast. The denser the beastfolk bloodline, the easier it becomes to comprehend that lifeform’s innate secret techniques.
Description: Blood Crystals can be stacked and used repeatedly to increase the concentration of one’s beastfolk bloodline.
After reading it, Daniel understood.
So Blood Crystals could actually be stacked.
Still, the idea of inheriting a creature’s bloodline by transforming into the form of that giant beast made him shudder.
He shook his head.
Turn himself into some savage beast in battle?
Absolutely impossible!
That would be far too ridiculous.
But those players probably would not care in the slightest.
The more something could increase their strength, the more eagerly they would rush toward it.
Even the ugliest and crudest form could be turned by them into the latest fashion trend.
The thought made him smile.
He then took out the second piece of loot.
[Gemstone (legendary-grade)]
Level: Tier 1
Rank: legendary-grade
Effects:
Universal auxiliary material. Gemstones increase the success rate of crafting and forging by 7%!
Universal energy material. Specific uses depend on the situation. Current energy reserve: S-rank.
Description: A specialty product of Aerial Realm. Gemstones come in nine colors; those of seven colors or above drop from legendary-grade creatures.
Daniel drew in a sharp breath.
This thing’s usefulness was far from simple!
First of all, it could increase the success rate of production for secondary classes.
That effect alone would be enough to make every player scramble for it!
Even if a single Gemstone were priced at one thousand gold coins, people would still fight over it and throw money at him. No matter how many he sold, there would always be buyers!
The second effect was even more outrageous!
Players might not yet understand what this meant, but Daniel had lived through previous lives and had personally experienced the Magitech Version.
At that time, mana crystals had already become Earth’s primary source of energy and industrial material. And because Aetheria’s mana crystal reserves were thin, their price had soared endlessly.
Yet mana crystals only had an A-rank energy reserve!
Gemstones, on the other hand, had an S-rank reserve. The two were not even on the same level!
Most importantly, this stuff could be regenerated endlessly!
With the Fourth Calamity in his hands, why would he ever worry about lacking output?
This was absolutely top-tier.
Daniel took a deep breath and stored the Gemstone away.
These first two drops alone had already satisfied him immensely.
And next came the grand finale—
[Beast Soul]!
A drifting, illusory mist-like shadow appeared in Daniel’s palm.
This was the Beast Soul!
[Beast Soul (legendary-grade)]
Level: Tier 1
Rank: legendary-grade
Effects:
A universal material for weapons and armor. After fusing with a Beast Soul, the base attributes of arms and armor can increase by 10% to 50%!
Fusing a Beast Soul can also make one’s own Beast Soul increasingly stronger.
Description: A drop from the lifeforms of Aerial Realm. A top-tier forging material. It can also be absorbed to improve the level and strength of one’s own Beast Soul.
A flicker passed through Daniel’s eyes.
The Hornless Rhino had indeed lived up to the description of being "treasure from head to toe."
The importance of this Beast Soul was in no way inferior to Gemstones or Blood Crystals.

And it complemented Blood Crystals perfectly: after using Blood Crystals, one had a chance to awaken the lifeform talent [Beast Soul], then use dropped Beast Souls to strengthen it—forming a perfect ecological cycle.
Most importantly, these beasts could all reproduce.
That meant this was a treasure trove that could be harvested without end!
And to excavate this treasure...
the best tools imaginable were those hundreds of millions of players, along with the army of legendary-grade powerhouses under his command.
As long as he arranged things properly, he could make a fortune without lifting a finger.
With that in mind, Daniel continued exploring Aerial Realm.
He flew across the boundless sea and discovered that sea beasts lurked in the depths of the ocean!
These sea beasts were also one branch of the realm’s lifeforms. Among them, the largest possessed transcendent legendary-grade strength, with bodies stretching for a hundred thousand meters.
He flew over towering mountain ranges.
Within those mountains were great numbers of lower-ranked lifeforms.
He deliberately stopped there and built several portals, just in case.
This world was still in its primal state, and traces of civilization were almost nowhere to be seen.
Only after he crossed plains and hills, rivers and mighty waterways...
did he finally discover the faint traces of civilization.
They were humanoid native inhabitants, still living primitive tribal lives.
These human tribes settled near mountains and rivers, surviving by hunting and gathering, and their lives were exceedingly harsh.
After all, the apex of Aerial Realm’s food chain was those countless powerful lifeforms.
They were the absolute overlords of this newborn world.
Compared to them, humanity was pitifully small.
Daniel flew across the entire world and discovered only a little over a thousand human tribes in total, and even the largest among them numbered only a little over a thousand people.
From that, it could be roughly estimated that the total human population within Aerial Realm was still under one million.
He pondered for a moment.
And in his heart, he had already come up with a fine way to rule Aerial Realm.

sentences.text: "Let’s first see how strong these native beasts really are."
This was Daniel’s first time coming into contact with these creatures, and he did not yet understand how they fought.
Understanding their combat patterns would determine how he would formulate grinding strategies for players in the future.
So he was in no hurry to make a move.
He deliberately lowered his altitude and hovered right in front of the beasts, looking at them the way one might inspect pigs or dogs.
At once, the caution in the lead Hornless Rhino’s eyes turned into towering fury.
A flash of blood-red light burst from its body as it charged straight at Daniel!
Its massive frame was unimaginably huge, and at this moment it came crashing forward like a mountain rolling over the earth.
Daniel remained in an observational state the entire time.
The instant the blood-red glow appeared on the Hornless Rhino, all its stats truly doubled.
"So this is how the beastfolk bloodline is used?"
At the same time—
"Flash!"
Whoosh—
Without the least hurry, he blinked a short distance away and lightly evaded the charge.
Roar!
Roar!
The Hornless Rhino flew into a rage and shook its body violently.
In the void, a phantom identical to its true form—but much smaller—suddenly appeared.
Whoosh—
The phantom shot toward Daniel like lightning, far lighter and far faster than the main body!
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Could this phantom be the [Beast Soul]?
"Not bad."
He smiled and teleported again.
No matter how the phantom pursued him, he could always dodge with ease.
A few minutes later, he felt that was enough.
This creature probably had no other attack methods left.
Daniel glanced at the Hornless Rhino below him, instantly summoned ninety-nine clones, and swung Stellar Wrath!
"Hunting Domain!"
"Shadowfont!"
"Wind’s Embrace!"
"Thunder Abyss!"
Boom—!
Boom—!
A deafening peal of thunder exploded as hundreds of forbidden spells poured down like a raging tide, instantly swallowing the colossal beast whole.
In barely the blink of an eye—
[Ding!
You have killed [Hornless Rhino], obtaining [Blood Crystal] ×10,000, [Gemstone] ×10,000, [Beast Soul] ×10,000!]
Hearing the system notification, Daniel took out the drops for a closer look.
After all, the Hornless Rhino’s description had not explained the true uses of these spoils in detail.
He first picked up a crimson crystal about the size of a pebble.

Effect: After use, there is a 1% chance of obtaining a [beastfolk bloodline], thereby gaining the corresponding race’s [Bloodline Inheritance].

The denser the beastfolk bloodline, the easier it becomes to comprehend that lifeform’s innate secret techniques.
Description: Blood Crystals can be stacked and used repeatedly to increase the concentration of one’s beastfolk bloodline.
After reading it, Daniel understood.
So Blood Crystals could actually be stacked.
Still, the idea of inheriting a creature’s bloodline by transforming into the form of that giant beast made him shudder.
He shook his head.
Turn himself into some savage beast in battle?
Absolutely impossible!
That would be far too ridiculous.
But those players probably would not care in the slightest.
The more something could increase their strength, the more eagerly they would rush toward it.
Even the ugliest and crudest form could be turned by them into the latest fashion trend.
The thought made him smile.

[Gemstone (legendary-grade)]
Level: Tier 1
Rank: legendary-grade
Effects:
Universal auxiliary material.
Gemstones increase the success rate of crafting and forging by 7%!
Universal energy material.
Specific uses depend on the situation.
Current energy reserve: S-rank.
Description: A specialty product of Aerial Realm.

That effect alone would be enough to make every player scramble for it!

No matter how many he sold, there would always be buyers!

Gemstones, on the other hand, had an S-rank reserve.
The two were not even on the same level!

This was absolutely top-tier.

chapters.title: Chapter 169 -169-Salvation! The Human Race’s Guide!
paragraphs: Blackstone Tribe.
Deep within the boundless mountain ranges,
hundreds of warriors clad in crude beast hides were fleeing for their lives, their faces filled with panic.
"Run! Run! We’ve enraged that giant beast!"
"That monster can shatter the earth with a single stomp and bring down forests with one roar—it’s far too terrifying!"
"We knew full well it was its territory. We never should have barged in... We’re finished now!"
The warriors were in utter disarray.
Yet amid the fleeing crowd, a group of young men pushed against the flow instead.
"Roger! What are you and your hunting party trying to do? Run now!"
"Don’t be reckless, Roger! That giant beast is absolutely not something we can kill. Hurry and leave!"
"That’s right! You may be the strongest warrior in the tribe, but you have no idea how powerful that beast really is! You’re no match for it!"
But the youths turned a deaf ear to the old hunters’ desperate warnings and instead strode forward toward the beast.
At the front, the young man named Roger wore a resolute expression as he shouted aloud,
"A warrior of the Blackstone Tribe would rather die in battle than retreat in disgrace! I’m going to challenge that giant beast!"
The moment his words fell, the young men at his side echoed him at once.
"That’s right! The Blackstone Tribe is invincible!"
"Roger has awakened a high-grade Beast Soul—I believe he’ll win!"
"I believe in Roger, just as I love this land!"
Ignoring all attempts to stop them, they pressed onward against the tide until they finally caught sight of the giant beast.
Its body was like an ancient mountain peak given life, and its two eyes blazed like twin suns hanging high in the heavens.
Roger showed no fear at all and gritted his teeth as he roared,
"Beastform!"
Roar—!
In an instant, Roger’s whole body underwent a violent transformation, turning into a gigantic beast!
Yet compared to the colossal monster before him, he was no more than an infant standing before a giant.
"Roar—!"
Roger bellowed and charged headlong toward the beast.
The monster swung a massive paw and sent him flying with a single slap.
Pfft!
Cough—
Blood gushed from Roger’s mouth, but he still refused to give up.
"Beast Soul!"
A phantom shot out from his body and lunged straight at the beast.
Roar! Roar—!
Disdain flashed through the giant beast’s eyes. It struck again, shattering the phantom with one blow.
Pfft—!
Roger’s Beast Soul instantly dimmed, and he himself spat out mouthfuls of blood. Unable to maintain his beastform any longer, he collapsed weakly to the ground.
The youths who had come with him immediately rushed forward to check his injuries.
"Cough... cough... I’m no match for it!"
"Don’t worry about me. Run..."
A trace of despair flashed through Roger’s eyes as he urged his companions to flee.
And at that very moment—
Boom!
Boom! Boom!
The giant beast strode toward them.
Each step made the earth tremble violently, as though mountains and land alike were shaking.
"This is bad—it’s too fast..."
"Our speed is nowhere near enough to outrun it... We’re all going to die here..."
Despair filled the faces of the young men.
Yet in that same instant—
Whoosh!
A figure suddenly appeared in front of them, blocking their path.
A faint smile played at Daniel’s lips as he looked at the enormous creature before him.
This giant beast was only low legendary-grade, nothing more.
He swung Stellar Wrath.
"Hunting Domain!"
"Shadowfont!"
"Wind’s Embrace!"
"Aetherlance!"
In an instant, the winds and clouds changed color.
Under Daniel’s control, countless meteors came crashing down upon the savage beast like a torrential storm.
In the blink of an eye, the giant beast was instantly slain!
Beasts without Immortal Singularities were laughably easy to kill.
As long as their life force was exhausted, they would die completely.
He did not even need to summon clones, nor could he be bothered to use forbidden spells.
[Ding! You have slain [Savage Colossus Bear], obtaining [Blood Crystal] ×10,000, [Gemstone] ×10,000, [Beast Soul] ×10,000!]
Daniel listened to the system prompt with an indifferent expression.
During his survey of Aerial Realm, he had already slain animals of all ranks.
Whether they were common-grade, epic-grade, legendary-grade, or even higher legendary-grade creatures, the number of drops had always been more or less the same.
In other words, if ordinary players came here to grind monsters, the base number of drops from each beast-type lifeform would remain the same.
He attributed this to the special nature of Aerial Realm.
After all, this was a newborn world.
He did not really mind either way. Once he harvested the materials from the players later and applied Millionfold Boost...
Heh.
While Daniel was thinking, the tribal youths behind him were staring at him with eyes filled with incomparable awe.
Roger was the boldest of them all. He dropped to his knees reverently.
"Honored god... have you come to save us?"
Daniel turned around and carefully examined the group of young men.
They were full of vitality, and what stood out most was their fearless, combative spirit.
He had already decided to cultivate a human agent—someone through whom he could establish an ideal civilization in this newborn land.
And these youths were the sparks in his hand.
At that thought, Daniel shook his head at Roger.
"No. I am not a god."
He smiled faintly, his voice ringing with strength.
"Because even gods... will one day be trampled beneath the feet of humanity."
"You may call me... the Guide."
Rustle—
All the young men dropped to their knees in unison and respectfully cried out,
"We pay our respects to Lord Guide!"
Daniel studied the tribal youths before him.
In the way they looked at him, five parts were devout worship, and the other five were deep reverence.
Establishing his authority had gone perfectly. The plan could begin.
With that thought, he waved his hand and took out ten thousand of each item—Blood Crystal, Gemstone, and Beast Soul—piling them up before the youths like small mountains.
Roger and his companions looked at the Guide in confusion.
Daniel said calmly,
"I want to make a trade with you."
"Agree to my terms, and all of these will be yours. They can grant you unparalleled Strength."
Roger lowered his head respectfully.
"Lord Guide, please command us."
Daniel’s voice was as calm as still water.
"With these, you will be able to grow stronger and seize a safe territory with ease."
Hearing that, Roger’s gaze fell upon the resources on the ground.
He had awakened a Beast Soul himself, so he naturally understood the value of these items.
Blood Crystals could allow people to grasp the source of Strength.
Gemstones could provide humanity with endless energy.
Beast Souls could make the tribe’s strongest even stronger.
With these things, the Blackstone Tribe truly had a chance to rise and become a dominant force!
Daniel took in every change in his expression and continued in the same calm tone.
"And the price for these is simple—"
"For every ten creatures you kill, you must hand over one portion of the materials you obtain as tribute to me."
Roger trembled with excitement and hurriedly bowed low.
"We will obey Lord Guide’s command! Thank you for your generosity!"
Though young, he understood what truly mattered.
If they could not obtain the resources before them, whether the tribe would even continue to exist was uncertain.
But with them, the tribe would inevitably flourish.
If not enough to dominate a region, it would at least gain the power to protect itself.
And once they secured a safe stretch of land, they would have a stable source of food.
With food, the tribe could multiply and grow.
It was the simplest calculation in the world.
The young men beside Roger also hurriedly voiced their agreement.
Seeing them accept, Daniel gave a slight nod.
Through a trade like this, he would be able to secure a stable stream of output from Aerial Realm even before the players had fully grown.
He possessed the Millionfold Boost talent. Anything that passed through his hands could be multiplied a millionfold!
If the million or so humans of Aerial Realm could continue to grow and prosper, then the quantity of items he would receive would become astronomical.
In the end, these native humans were nothing more than leeks he had carefully planted.
From beginning to end, all he had invested was a mere ten thousand drops from legendary-grade monsters.
And in return, he would receive a never-ending stream of human production across endless years.
At present, the native human population numbered less than a million—
but what about in the future, when they reached ten million? A hundred million?
By then, the resources he harvested would fill an entire world.

chapters.title: Chapter 170 -170-His Majesty the Emperor Really Has Good Sense
paragraphs: Other than these native human players, the players as a whole were Daniel’s next crop to harvest.

At present, players still lacked the strength to contend with legendary-grade monsters, but dealing with lower-tier creatures was more than manageable for them. If they were organized properly, even surrounding and killing Exalted-grade monsters would not be impossible.
If he had to wait for the players to grow on their own, that would be far too slow.
But that was not a problem. Daniel still had the supreme treasure known as the Phantom Emporium in his hands.
Its core function was simple: it could accelerate the growth of players at a terrifying pace.

With it, the players’ strength would soar by leaps and bounds, almost changing with each passing day. And with the player population’s frightening efficiency when it came to grinding monsters, they were something the native inhabitants of this world simply could not compare to.
No matter how things developed, Daniel was destined to make an enormous profit—enough to fill his coffers to overflowing.
After finalizing many of the details with Roger and the others, Daniel no longer had any reason to stay.
His exploration of the Aerial Realm was already nearing its end.
This newborn world was like a blank sheet of paper that had yet to bear a single stroke of ink. In the future, it might be worth visiting from time to time.
Meanwhile, Roger returned to the Blackstone Tribe, carrying with him the hope of the tribe’s rise.
After returning, he reported every detail of his journey and of how he had received guidance, recounting it all to the tribe’s elders without omission.
When the elders saw the mountain of supplies piled before them, they had no choice but to believe that everything Roger said was true.
So the strongest being in this world was called Wayfarer.
And Daniel, too, was a human.
Unlike the hot-blooded youths, the elders were far calmer and more cautious. They treasured Daniel’s existence beyond measure.
In their eyes, Daniel was the guardian of humankind.
Thus, they made a decision on the spot: from this day forward, the protective deity of the Blackstone Tribe would be replaced by Wayfarer.
First, they established the Sanctum of the Wayfarer.
Then, based on the youths’ descriptions of Wayfarer’s appearance, they carved a stone statue and enshrined it within the sanctuary.
Once all of that was completed, the tribe designated this day as the grandest festival of the year and named it Revelation Day.
After everything was prepared, the tribal chief gathered together the strongest young warriors of the clan and began using Blood Crystals to awaken the beastfolk bloodline within them.
At the same time, those who had already awakened their Beast Soul were made to devour additional Beast Souls to further enhance their strength.
After that, they used Gemstones to forge incomparably sharp weapons.
Some time later, the Blackstone Tribe rose with astonishing speed, becoming the most powerful tribe within a thousand-mile radius.
The number of beasts and monsters they hunted increased day by day.
At the same time, they never forgot the promise they had made to Wayfarer.
For every ten monster drops they obtained, they would always set aside one portion and place it within the Sanctum of the Wayfarer, waiting for the day when Wayfarer would descend once more.
Daniel had already returned to Aetheria.
The Polaris District, Imperial City.
The moment Daniel returned to the Imperial City, the upper echelon under his command came to seek an audience with him.
The first to speak was Carodion, Master of the Temple of the Gods.
"My King," Carodion said slowly, "the Temple of the Gods has received two advancement slots to supreme-grade. How would you like them to be assigned?"
Supreme-grade experts?
Daniel’s eyes lit up at once.
After the new version had gone live, as the number one power in the region, the imperial faction would naturally receive slots allowing experts to advance to supreme-grade.
That had always been the case in his previous lives.
But things were different now.
Daniel now stood at the apex of the world, and the greatest beneficiary of those supreme-grade slots would naturally be himself.
Unlike in his previous lives, when the appearance—or absence—of supreme-grade experts had nothing to do with him.
Daniel pondered for a moment.
At present, the Temple of the Gods had several hundred legendary-grade experts. But when it came to closeness and loyalty, Carodion and Aliris were unquestionably the foremost among them.
He barely hesitated.
"Then you and Aliris will be the first to advance to supreme-grade."
Carodion replied in his usual steady tone, "Thank you, my King, for your grace."
Daniel nodded. "Once I finish dealing with the backlog of affairs that’s piled up recently, I’ll take you to the Aerial Realm."
"In the future, we’ll rotate the legendary-grade experts in there so they can hunt monsters and improve their strength."
At the moment, those legendary-grade experts had nothing much to do anyway. Since they were idle, sending them to the Aerial Realm as laborers was not a bad arrangement.
"As you command, my King."
Carodion bowed and withdrew.
Yet what surprised Daniel was that the next visitor turned out to be an envoy sent by the Emperor of World Zone No. 616.
And the Emperor had sent a generous gift along with him.

The envoy bowed respectfully and said, "Lord Faustus, His Majesty sent me here to ask for your guidance. Regarding the two supreme-grade advancement slots belonging to the Temple of the Gods in World Zone No. 616—how do you wish to assign them?"
Daniel was briefly taken aback, but he quickly understood.
Right now, his status in the Polaris District was supreme and unshakable. The same was true in World Zone No. 616.
Even the Emperor did not dare grant supreme-grade titles on his own. Matters of this scale had to be left for Daniel to decide.
After all, no one understood Daniel’s importance better than the Emperor of World Zone No. 616.
Daniel did not stand on ceremony.
Naturally, supreme-grade slots should be reserved for those closest to him.
Smiling, he said, "Go back and convey my thanks to His Majesty."
"As for the Temple of the Gods’ two supreme-grade advancement slots, give them to Irene and Ier."
Those two were the very experts he had revived after the battle against Baal, the ruler of the shadowkin. Back then, they had only been legendary-grade high-grade.
But with the steady stream of resources Daniel had supplied, they had now already advanced to transcendent legendary-grade.
"As you wish, Lord Faustus."
The envoy tactfully withdrew and hurried back to World Zone No. 616.
Watching the envoy’s departing figure, Daniel found himself in an excellent mood.
As expected, after everything he had done for World Zone No. 616, His Majesty the Emperor really did have excellent sense.
Across two World Zones, all four supreme-grade advancement slots had fallen into his hands.
It felt incredible.

Once the mainstream players reached level 200 and the World War fully erupted, he could kill the supreme-grade experts from other World Zones, revive them, and gain yet another batch of supreme-grade and legendary-grade powerhouses for himself.
And there was another point worth noting: other races on Aetheria now possessed supreme-grade experts as well.
Daniel had already set his sights on them.
If he could grasp the life and death of those non-human races in the palm of his hand, then would those supreme-grade experts among the non-human races dare do anything except obey him?
That way, he could build an entire army of supreme-grade experts.
That was also the confidence behind his willingness to oppose the Godkin.
No matter how many legendary-grade experts the Godkin sent down, they would only be delivering themselves to him.
Besides, this world simply could not withstand the descent of Divine-grade experts. Even supreme-grade experts could not descend in large numbers.
And if only a limited number could come?
Then he would kill however many came.
For the time being, everything was still relatively stable. He could not be bothered to waste energy guessing what schemes those Godkin bastards were plotting.
At the end of the day, nothing mattered more than making his own foundation as solid as possible.
With that thought, Daniel leaned back against his chair and spoke lazily.
"Next."
"Alan seeks an audience."
The instant Daniel heard that name, his expression turned serious.
Alan was in charge of matters concerning the players within the Doom Legion. He was bound to be carrying all kinds of strange and unusual developments brought about by the new version.
Daniel immediately became interested.

chapters.title: Chapter 171 -171-The Night Belongs to Another World
paragraphs: "Your subject Alan greets you, my King."
Alan bowed with perfect formality.
Daniel did not bother with small talk. "Speak. What is it?"
Alan drew a deep breath.
Everything under his charge revolved around players, including those from the former World Zone No. 1213. This was the area Daniel had always watched most closely.
During this period, Alan had followed Daniel’s instructions to the letter and had already achieved considerable results.
"Following your orders, my King, more than ninety percent of the players from the former World Zone No. 1213 have now been converted into life-class professions."
"There are still a few stubborn ones left. We’ve been beating them down hard. In my judgment, before long there won’t be a single combat-class player left among them."
After hearing this, a faint smile rose at the corner of Daniel’s lips.
Turning all the former players of World Zone No. 1213 into life-class professionals had been his plan from the very beginning.
There were more than a billion of them.
Once players were allowed to grow unchecked, they became increasingly difficult to control. If they were left to develop freely underground, sooner or later they would become a serious problem.
So the simplest and most effective solution was to completely sever their ambition to walk the path of combat and force them all into life-class professions instead.
That way, they would lose all capital to make trouble.
The more than one billion players of World Zone No. 1213 would become his permanent labor force—ripe for harvesting whenever he pleased.
Daniel nodded. "What about those undead?"

Alan smiled as he replied, "My King, the undead passageway in World Zone No. 1213 is currently guarded by more than a dozen epic-grade elite regiments from the Polaris Legion. Their retreat route has been sealed completely."
He paused, then continued, "Right now, those undead have become living targets for adventurers to grind levels and farm treasures from. They can be handled however we like."
Daniel gave a mild hum in acknowledgment.

Back when the Undead Cataclysm had raged through World Zone No. 1213, Daniel had not rushed to exterminate all the undead after taking over that territory. The reason was simple: he intended to keep them alive like a crop, saving them for players to reap.
To prevent the undead from escaping back into the Undead Realm, he had stationed troops to block every avenue of retreat.
Now those undead had long since become training dummies for the players of World Zone No. 616 and the Polaris District.
Using a natural disaster as a farmable crop—there was probably not a second player in gaming history who had ever done something like that.
Daniel nodded in satisfaction. "Well done."
"Now then—how far have you gotten in gathering information on the new version?"
The moment Alan heard that, his expression changed abruptly, becoming unusually grave.
"My King, we’ve collected quite a lot of information about the new version... but all of it seems highly abnormal."
Abnormal?
Daniel frowned and gestured for him to continue.
Alan said, "Every night, mysterious sounds begin ringing in the ears of adventurers."
"Mysterious sounds? What kind of sounds?"
Daniel’s brows drew together more tightly.

After thinking for a moment, Alan explained, "Some people say they hear the calls of a bustling marketplace. Others say they hear the murmured conversations of a family sitting together. Some hear the noise of cups being raised and set down inside a tavern."
He continued, "Even stranger, some people claim they hear the clash of swords on a battlefield, or the cries of wild beasts."
There was astonishment in Alan’s voice. "And it isn’t just one or two people saying this. Nearly every adventurer can hear something unnatural."
"However, according to the information we’ve collected, none of these sounds can be heard near an Ancestral Temple or an Ancestral Statue."
Daniel let out a low sound of interest. "Oh? What’s so special about the Ancestral Temple and the Ancestral Statue?"
"They are special," Alan said with certainty.

Then he continued, "A great many adventurers have personally seen that, at night, the Ancestral Statues emit glowing figures identical to the stone statues themselves. Those figures roam around in the middle of the night carrying weapons—and those weapons are stained with blood."
"Now that is interesting."
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
The purpose of an Ancestral Statue was, in the first place, to protect the clan.
If these statues were coming alive at night and patrolling with blood on their weapons...
Did that mean they were automatically cutting down anything hostile to humankind?
The strange behavior of the Ancestral Statues, together with those mysterious sounds, was indeed thought-provoking.
Daniel asked, "Have you reached any conclusions?"
Alan hesitated briefly before answering, "We have reached one conclusion, but... it sounds rather unbelievable."
Daniel smiled. "That’s fine. Say it."
Alan spoke slowly and clearly, enunciating every word.
"We believe one of the secrets of the new version is this—the night in this world belongs to another world."
Boom—!
Daniel felt his mind tremble.
It was as though he had understood something—and yet understood nothing at all.
Strange sounds. Moving statues. The night belonging to another world?
He blinked.
Could this be one of the true faces of the new version?
At that thought, he took a deep breath.
"Excellent. You’ve done very well."
Then he added, "Keep digging into these secrets. Do not overlook a single clue."
Alan bowed respectfully. "As you command, my King."
As Daniel watched Alan’s retreating figure, light flickered in his eyes.
So the new version of the game was this interesting?
It had actually created an entirely second world?
Only, this world overlapped with the main world, divided by day and night.
It seemed he would have to go and investigate it personally.
With that thought, Daniel directly took out the Phantom Emporium.
At the moment, this item was of the utmost importance.
His class change quest required him to cultivate one hundred Holywing Angels.
That meant he absolutely needed sufficiently powerful players to serve as the backbone.
And the Phantom Emporium was precisely the perfect tool for allowing players to rapidly grow stronger.
What was more, the Aerial Realm was also waiting for players to mature as quickly as possible.

The Phantom Emporium before him was capable of producing tens of thousands of different phantoms. Their strength could be adjusted freely, with the maximum reaching transcendent legendary-grade, and they refreshed once every sixty minutes.
If the level of the Phantom Emporium was raised, the refresh time could be shortened.
Not only that, after being upgraded, the number of these Emporiums would increase from one to several.
Daniel directly pulled out the Phantom Emporium and checked the conditions required for upgrading it. It required sacrificing ten legendary-grade companion eggs.
Then he remembered the mountain of World War Points still in his possession.
"I’ve got more than enough World War Points left."
Daniel immediately exchanged a large batch of legendary-grade companion eggs with his points.
[ Ding! Do you wish to use legendary-grade companion eggs to upgrade the Phantom Emporium? ]
"Confirm!"
[ Ding! The Phantom Emporium has been upgraded successfully. Current level: Level 10. ]
In one breath, Daniel pushed the Phantom Emporium all the way to max level.
After reaching max level, the item could deploy ten Emporiums simultaneously, and the refresh time had been reduced from sixty minutes to once every six minutes.
Only after finishing all that did he leave the imperial palace.
He placed five Phantom Emporiums in the Polaris District and another five in World Zone No. 616, adjusting the phantoms’ level and grade to the range most comfortable for players to grind.
He also set an admission fee and restricted access so that only guild members could use them.
That way, he could lightly fleece the players for another round of profit while simultaneously allowing his guild members to level up at astonishing speed.
And once the players grew stronger in the future, the difficulty of this item could be increased again.
By the time Daniel had finished placing the Emporiums and sent out the guild-wide announcement, the sky was already growing dark.
"Perfect timing," he murmured. "Let’s see what kind of unspeakable things are hidden in the night."

chapters.title: Chapter 172 -172-An Ancient Bracelet and a Hidden Instance
paragraphs: Night had fallen completely.
Daniel stood alone atop a solitary hill on the outskirts of Imperial City.
The night wind howled around him, tugging at his robes and hair until they snapped loudly in the air.
He remained motionless, simply waiting.
Alan had said that once night fell, players would begin hearing strange noises, and the Ancestral Statues would also start behaving oddly.
The conclusion they had reached was this: the world of the new version had been layered together, with day and night each belonging to a different world.
Daytime belonged to Aetheria, but the night belonged to another mysterious realm that no one could clearly define.
Just as he was thinking about it, Daniel’s ears twitched slightly.
It was here—that strange noise!
Buzz... rustle... whisper...
A jumble of chaotic sounds rushed into his ears all at once.
The noises came and went in fits, yet seemed to follow some hidden code.
Some dragged on for a long time, some ended sharply and abruptly, some were so loud they were startling, while others were as thin and faint as the buzz of a mosquito.
For the moment, he could not make out what kind of scenes these sounds belonged to.
He frowned.
What exactly was the point of creating an overlapping world like this in the new version?
Could the secret of the Flame of Heritage be hidden within this chaotic tangle of sounds?
He could not figure it out for the time being.
But he did notice one thing—he could see vague shadows floating around him.
Within his field of vision, dim figures flickered in and out of existence, just like the sounds, appearing only sporadically.
"So I’m the only one who can see them? Why did Alan never mention this?"
Daniel found himself puzzled.
Those phantoms resembled an ink-wash landscape painting. At times they formed the outline of a city, and at other times they became bustling streets full of people moving back and forth.
But everything was too blurry to see clearly.
It felt as though he were standing at the center of a stage surrounded on all sides by illusions.
Daniel patiently continued watching.
At that moment, a light suddenly appeared in the distance.
Daniel’s pupils contracted sharply.
The light grew clearer and clearer. It turned out to be a phantom projected by an Ancestral Statue.
The figure was shrouded in a faint white glow. It seemed to be a knight, gripping a long spear and galloping forward on horseback.
But after racing for a while, the statue’s phantom suddenly vanished into thin air.
Daniel watched helplessly as the figure plunged headlong into the darkness and disappeared without a trace.
Gone?
Yet not long after, that same light reappeared from another direction.
It was still the same phantom knight of the Ancestral Statue, riding back with imposing majesty.
With his keen eyesight, Daniel clearly saw that the tip of the spear was indeed still stained with fresh blood, exactly as Alan had described.
And just then, a phantom suddenly darted right in front of Daniel.
Every hair on his body stood on end.
It was the phantom of a little girl, no more than ten or so years old, staring at him with wide, curious eyes.
Daniel widened his own eyes and stared right back at her.
They were so close that it felt as though one could touch the other simply by reaching out.
After hesitating for a moment, the little girl slowly extended her hand.
Her eyes were filled with curiosity as she gradually raised her arm and reached her palm forward.
Daniel did not move.
The hand in the phantom kept reaching forward—and passed straight through his body.
The little girl looked shocked, her eyes filled with disbelief.
Her lips moved as if she were saying something, but Daniel could not hear a single word.
The scene was bizarre beyond words, as if living beings from two separate worlds were tentatively probing each other through an invisible wall.
Daniel drew a deep breath and tried reaching out as well.
The result was the same as with the girl—his hand passed straight through empty air.
At that moment, the little girl seemed to hear something. A look of urgency immediately appeared on her face.
She turned to glance at Daniel, then gritted her teeth, pulled a bracelet from her wrist, and threw it down by his feet before turning and running off, vanishing without a trace.
Daniel blinked, then lowered his gaze to the bracelet and cast a detection spell on it.
[Unknown Bracelet (???)]
"Hm? This is..."
To his surprise, the bracelet could actually be detected.
That meant it was a real, tangible object.
He bent down and picked it up.
Sure enough, it felt cool in his hand. Its design was similar to the jewelry of Aetheria, except that it looked exceptionally old and worn.
"Is this a quest item? Something from the other world? Or some kind of token?"
Clutching the bracelet, Daniel’s mind filled with questions.
Just then, the activity in the guild channel pulled him back to reality.
[Doom Guild Channel]
"Polaris District coordinates (91911, 46641). There’s a cave here. I just saw an Ancestral Statue’s phantom going in and out of it several times. Something’s definitely off!"
"Are you insane? You still dare go wandering around outside at night? None of us even dare step out after dark anymore."
"Holy shit, man, your guts are unreal. A few members have already been killed these past two days without understanding what happened."
"Exactly. I heard that over in World Zone No. 616, a few members got killed tonight too. Even the death notifications were vague and unclear."
"No, wait, why are you all talking about this creepy stuff like it’s normal? This is a game!!"
"Come on. Do you seriously still think this is just an ordinary game?"
"...In the real world, my Strength is high enough to punch straight through a wall..."
Daniel swept his gaze over the guild channel.
Most of the members were discussing the strange events of the night.
Players had actually been killed for no apparent reason.
Of course, that cave at the posted coordinates was strange as well.
What exactly was inside that cave that made the Ancestral Statue’s phantom run there again and again?
He opened the map and entered the coordinates.
The location was near a small town in the northernmost part of the Polaris District.
Daniel took a single step forward, and his entire body vanished from where he stood.
Whoosh—!
He appeared in front of the cave entrance.
By now, quite a few guild members had already gathered there.
The moment they saw Daniel appear, they became excited and started greeting him one after another.
"Holy shit, they actually called the guild leader over!"
"Leader, this cave’s seriously weird."
"No kidding. Once night falls, this place feels haunted as hell. Could it be some vampire instance inside?"
Daniel nodded and asked curiously, "What strange things have happened here?"
One of the members said, "A bunch of human-shaped phantoms keep appearing here. They show up and disappear at random, and whenever they appear, they bare their fangs and claws at us."
"And the Ancestral Statue’s phantom has been running back and forth here many times too. Something is obviously wrong."
Daniel asked, "Have you gone inside to look?"
"Of course we have."
Another person answered, "All of us have gone in several times already, but we didn’t find anything. The cave isn’t even very big—you hit the end after walking for just a few minutes."
Daniel nodded.
Even though no one else had found anything, he still wanted to go in and see for himself.
"Leader, are you going in? Can we come with you?"
"Yeah, Leader, take us along so we can broaden our horizons!"
"We probably won’t be much help, but just being able to follow the leader is good enough!"
Faced with the members’ requests, Daniel gave it a moment’s thought and agreed.
After all, they were all brothers from his own guild, not outsiders.
Besides, they had already gone in many times without discovering any real danger. Even if he went in himself, there was no guarantee he would encounter anything.
With that thought, he nodded.
"Alright."
"Holy shit! The leader’s taking us into an instance!"
"The leader is invincible!"
"We finally get a chance to witness the guild leader’s style again!"
"You’re overthinking it. We’re just going in to take a look, not to fight anything."

chapters.title: Chapter 173 -173-A Strange World and the Girl
paragraphs: Daniel glanced at the cave and led several hundred guild members inside in a long procession.
Everyone followed behind him without daring to act out of line. Even their voices were kept low, as though they were afraid of disturbing him.
Once they entered the cave, the starlight disappeared, and the darkness around them deepened.
"Light Spell!"
A quick-reacting priest cast a spell at once, illuminating the entire cave in bright light.
At first glance, the cave looked completely ordinary.
Bzzz—!
Just then, a deep humming sound suddenly rang out beside everyone’s ears.
"Hm? What’s that sound?"
"What the hell is that?"
"Look! The space ahead is changing... no, wait—it’s rippling!"
Daniel was walking at the very front.
In his vision, the space ahead had looked like the surface of a calm lake, but now ripples were suddenly spreading across it.
Wave after wave expanded outward.
What was going on?
He frowned and reached his hand toward the rippling space.
[Ding! You have discovered the hidden instance: Ancient Echo. Enter?]
The system notification sounded in his ears.
He did not choose immediately. Instead, he turned back and asked, "Did all of you get the system prompt too?"
The guild members behind him answered one after another.
"We got it! Looks like it’s a hidden instance!"
"Yeah, it’s called Ancient Echo!"
"Leader, are you the chosen one or something? We’ve gone in and out of this cave so many times and never triggered anything, but the moment you show up, the instance appears!"
"WTF! As expected of the man who monopolized the entire Stellar announcement board!"
"Leader, are we going in?"
The corner of Daniel’s lips curved up slightly as he replied coolly, "Of course."
Even as he said that, however, he was wondering inwardly.
Why had the instance triggered the moment he arrived, while the guild members who had gone in and out so many times had never encountered it?
He could not help but think of the strange ancient bracelet he had picked up earlier outside Imperial City.
Could it have something to do with that?
He shook his head and cast the distracting thoughts aside.
Since they had stumbled upon a hidden instance, there was no reason not to go in and see what it contained.
"I’d like to see for myself what secrets are hidden inside this instance."
Without hesitation, he selected Enter.
Whoosh—!
In the blink of an eye, Daniel and the several hundred guild members behind him vanished from the spot.
Whoosh—!
The sound of rushing wind filled Daniel’s ears.
He was falling—plummeting straight downward.
If he just let himself keep falling like this, who knew where he would end up?
"Voidstep!"
He quickly activated the skill to steady himself and slowly descended.
Strange.
It was currently night in Aetheria, yet here it was broad daylight, with the sun shining brilliantly overhead.
Even stranger, the guild members had not landed with him. Judging by the situation, they had likely been teleported elsewhere.
Daniel scanned the surroundings and soon noticed something.
Not far away, a barefoot little girl in plain clothes sat by the lakeside, her face sallow as she gazed at him blankly.
Daniel slowly walked over and asked, "Where is this place?"
The girl blinked and answered timidly, "This is Soul Devouring Vale."
Soul Devouring Vale?
Daniel frowned. "What’s your name?"
The girl replied haltingly, "My name is Kelly. What about you?"
Daniel was a little surprised. This little girl was bolder than he had expected—she had actually asked him in return.
He smiled faintly. "My name is Faustus. A human—Faustus."
He deliberately emphasized the words human.
After years of playing the game, he knew that the new version was inseparably tied to humankind. Those two words—human—might very well be the key to triggering a hidden quest.
Yet when Kelly heard the word human, she showed no particular reaction. She merely fell silent.
Daniel blinked.
So the keyword did not work?
Perhaps the timing was wrong, or perhaps the way quests were triggered in this instance was simply different from elsewhere.
So he casually found a rock and sat down, then probed further. "Kelly, why are you here all by yourself?"
Kelly lowered her head, as though remembering something unpleasant, and her mood visibly darkened.
In a small voice, she said, "Nobody here wants to play with me, so I can only play by myself."
Then she suddenly looked up and revealed a smile.
"But I’ve discovered lots of interesting places around here."
Interesting places?
Daniel felt as though he had caught onto something and immediately asked, "Can you tell me about them?"
"Of course!"
Kelly nodded earnestly.
"I found that in the morning, the forest not only has the most flowers, it’s also the place where rainbows appear the most often."
Daniel smiled. "That must be beautiful."
Seeing that the young man in front of her showed no impatience, Kelly grew more enthusiastic.
"And also, the afternoon is the most interesting time here. The lake water is warm, and the wind feels all soft and gentle."
"Then at night, the most beautiful place is the cliff over there. From there, you can see the roundest moon, and so many fireflies."
As Daniel listened, he was simultaneously pondering whether each of her words concealed clues that might trigger a quest.
At that moment, Kelly suddenly shot out her hand and grabbed at the air.
"Hey! Guess what I caught?"
"What?"
"A gift. I want to give it to you."
Kelly grinned, revealing a row of neat white teeth.
Daniel smiled. "Then I’d like to see it."
Kelly smiled as she slowly opened her palm.
A rainbow rested in her hand.
When Daniel had first entered the instance, his mind had been full of quests. How could he possibly have paid attention to something like a rainbow?
If Kelly had not seemed like the kind of NPC who could trigger a quest, he would have run out of patience long ago.
His expression sharpened slightly, though the smile on his face did not change. "Thank you, Kelly."
Kelly smiled. "You really are just like the legend says."
"Hm? A legend?"
"Yes!"
"In the legend, there’s a monster living in Soul Devouring Vale. It can turn into anyone’s appearance, become friends with anyone, and then, when they least expect it, swallow them whole."
She looked at Daniel with some fear in her eyes.
"If you want to eat me... could you swallow me in one bite? I’m afraid it would hurt."
At those words, the smile slowly vanished from Daniel’s face.
The monster of Soul Devouring Vale? Eating people?
Kelly had mistaken him for the monster from the legend?
Caught between amusement and disbelief, he shook his head. "I’m not a monster. I’m not even from this place."
Kelly froze for a moment, then suddenly burst into laughter.
"Hahaha, you’re saying you’re not from this place?"
"Then what world are you from? The God Realm? The Demon Realm? The Undead Realm? The world of the sea demons?"
Daniel was startled inwardly.
He realized Kelly seemed remarkably familiar with the various worlds of different races.
Could this hidden instance be a world where many races lived together?
He shook his head. "I’m not from any of those places. I’m human, just like you."
Then, curious, he asked, "This monster of Soul Devouring Vale you mentioned—what exactly is it?"
Kelly looked at him in confusion. "This place is Soul Devouring Vale. Soul Devouring Vale belongs to the Soul Devourers."
"They decree that every major human city must send three hundred children into the valley each year for them to eat. Otherwise, they’ll go to war with humankind."
A trace of sorrow surfaced in her eyes.
"And I... am one of the sacrifices they selected."
Boom—!
Daniel’s eyes flew wide open.
A sacrifice!
He felt a rush of hot blood shoot straight to his head, and his anger surged violently upward.

chapters.title: Chapter 174 -174-Wrath — The Destruction of the Soul Devourers!
paragraphs: The moment Kelly finished speaking, a system notification suddenly exploded in Daniel’s ears.
[Ding! You have triggered a hidden instance quest. Please guide "Kelly" into revealing her origins.]
[Hint: A new quest has been added to your quest log. Please check it for details!]
With a dark expression, Daniel opened his quest log.
[Kelly’s Origins (Side Quest)] (Hidden Instance)
Quest Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Objective: Investigate the secrets of the hidden instance and guide "Kelly" into revealing her origins to unlock the next stage of the story.
Time Limit: 9:57:40
Daniel closed the quest log. When he looked at Kelly again, his gaze had completely changed.
If this girl could serve as the key to an instance quest, then it meant she was deeply tied to whatever came next. She might even be an extremely important character.
A smoldering anger rose in his chest as he asked her,
"What about your parents? They just abandoned you?"
He truly could not understand how any parent could throw away their own child like this.
Kelly gave a bitter smile.
Her eyes were red as she lifted her head to look at the sky. The wind brushed past, stirring the loose strands of hair on her forehead.
"Mom and Dad said they were taking me to a big city to have fun," she said, her voice trembling slightly. "They said they’d buy me lots of delicious food."
"But they couldn’t fool me."
"I already knew they wanted to leave me there alone, so someone could take me here."
"I just didn’t expose them, because I knew that no matter how much I cried or made a fuss, it wouldn’t change anything. So I could only pretend I knew nothing."
"Then they told me to wait while they went to buy food for me. I knew... once they left, they would never come back."
"I hoped they wouldn’t blame themselves too much because of me. I wanted to leave them with the happiest version of me... so that would be the one they remembered forever."
"After that, I was brought here and left to wait for the Soul Devourers to come."
Kelly suddenly turned her head, looked at Daniel, and grinned.
"Don’t you think adults are stupid? They always think kids don’t know anything. But actually, I know everything."
Daniel finally understood.
"So that’s why you mistook me for a Soul Devourer?"
Kelly smiled awkwardly.
Daniel laughed as well and slowly got to his feet.
"Don’t worry. Even if the Soul Devourers come, there’s nothing to fear."
"From this moment on, no matter how many of them come, I’ll kill every last one."
"I mean it."
Kelly’s eyes sparkled. She nodded hard.
At that very moment—

[Soulreaving Moment (Quest Chain)] (Hidden Instance)
Quest Rank: Exalted-grade
Objectives:
Slay the Soul Devourers and rescue the sacrificed human civilians; Escort "Kelly" to "Starlight City."
Quest Description:
During the quest, Kelly’s power will continue to evolve. You must ensure her safety at all times. She must not die or suffer serious injury, and under no circumstances may she come to dislike you.
